I've been ordering from them for months, and visiting their physical café for the first time today helped me understand why their food/drinks are always so delicious and filled with warmth! It's owned by a very humble and cute couple who work incredibly hard. Not only that, but they also pay attention to every detail. Knowing that everything is organic and the place is so clean, I will definitely keep ordering from them!

Thank you for your hard work and the little gestures that definitely make my day better 🤎
sample_reviews_en.author: Irina Chus

sample_reviews_en.text:
While scrolling through bougie hipster cafes and overpriced breakfast locales, we happened to walk past this place on a random corner of the neighborhood and stepped in. It is small, cozy, and the quality to price and portion is the best I've had so far in Bangkok. The coffee and wraps and smoothies are beyond good, and it's a wonderfully humble little place where locals also seem to come; not much English being spoken around us.

Do yourself a favor and come by for breakfast. Best place in town
sample_reviews_en.author: Ryan Elliott

sample_reviews_en.text:
What a fantastic restaurant.
The food is organic, fresh and cooked with care and love.
Owners were lovely, sharing details about their food and teaching us about Thailand.
We had some pita sandwiches that were absolutely amazing, and the mango smoothie is a must!

Also: they use much less plastic than most places in Bangkok!! Extra points for this!! 💛

As a vegetarian, they had a tofu option that was delicious!

Will definitely be going back!
sample_reviews_en.author: Lili GG

sample_reviews_en.text:
Highly recommended, the 10 minute walk from the top of Soi 3 is well worth the effort. Owner managed by a Thai  husband and wife team (English speaking) this venue is sure to please.
Freshly prepared salads,  home baked cakes, and home made yoghurt smoothies are the best I’ve had in Bangkok.
If the walk is too much of an effort, delivery service is available.

The decor is fresh and clean with air conditioned comfort.
sample_reviews_en.author: Peter Williams

sample_reviews_en.text:
If i am in dindaeng and i need  something healthy, i always try to hit this place up. The owners are very friendly and the salads are always fresh and tasty. The coffee is good as are the soups.
The restaurant itself is quite small but very cozy. I would not bring a lot of people in here, but it's a great place to order take away or take a break from the heat for a quick bite. I love the plants and decorations.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ramsey Ramsey

sample_reviews_en.text: Gorgeous little place. Needed just a little something to eat and found this place via grab. Had a healthy brownie and a yoghurt smoothie for 100 baht. Incredibly tasty, and beautifully presented. The smoothie was so thick I ate it with a spoon, and the brownie was perfect as I don't have a sweet tooth and it's sugar free. If i wasn't leaving this morning, I'd be back at lunchtime.
sample_reviews_en.author: Tatum Triggs

restaurants.name: Raan Jay Fai
restaurants.address:

327 Maha Chai Rd, Samran Rat, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text: It did not measure to a ฿1500 experience for an omelette.  There was indeed a ton of crab, but the flavour was only ok. They only accept cash — no Prompt Pay like the rest of the city.  No customizing to make it pet mak mak. No soy sauce, only fish sauce in Kikkoman bottles (I think there are some intellectual property issues here).  And the kicker; they’ve received accolades from Michelin in the past, but no pictures with the chef due to health concerns. This is 2026 not 2020.  😞
sample_reviews_th.author: Brent Robertson

sample_reviews_en.text:
Timing
We arrived at 4:45 PM and got in line.
We were seated at around 6:15 PM, and the food was served at 6:55 PM.

Food
This is not just an omelet — most of the dish is actually crab meat, and the same goes for the other dishes, which are largely made from the main ingredient.
All the food is cooked over fire. The taste is excellent, with very tender crab.

Atmosphere
First, you stand in line; then someone comes to you with the menu, and you place a preliminary order. When you’re seated, you can additionally order drinks and rice. The wait is quite comfortable. The place has a clean restroom.

Overall Impression
Jay Fai is a legend. She personally cooks every dish, and you can feel her strong energy. She works non-stop for 10 hours to serve every guest. It’s impressive.
Some people left before their turn, and that was a mistake.
If they’ve taken your pre-order, you will definitely be served.
I also noticed that people were arriving at 7 PM, and they were still seated and had their orders taken without a long wait.
I don’t see the point of coming very early — you can come at any time, and the waiting time will be more or less the same.
sample_reviews_en.author: Igor

sample_reviews_en.text:
I was nearby and noticed there were only five people in line, so I decided to queue up. From waiting to ordering, eating, and paying, the whole experience took about one hour.

I keep seeing people leave bad reviews about the food just because they waited too long. That makes no sense to me. I’m only judging what was actually on my plate.

What I had was an insanely crispy omelette — perfectly crunchy on the outside, juicy inside, and generously packed with crab meat. Anyone who says this doesn’t taste good simply has no understanding of food. You cannot mix the hype or the waiting time into the evaluation of the dish itself. You should judge only what ends up on the plate — and that was a solid 10/10.

Yes, the price is crazy. Everyone knows it’s overpriced. But Jay Fai is a brand now — and she actually stands at the wok herself, unlike many Michelin restaurants where the chef barely shows up and maybe greets guests once a week.

Is it ridiculously expensive, especially in a city where you can eat well for three euros? Absolutely.
Was it the most delicious crab omelette I’ve ever had? Also absolutely yes.
sample_reviews_en.author: DJ Mosaken

sample_reviews_en.text:
Made this an ultimate food destination in our must-go-to list since watching Somebody Feed Phil's pilot episode from years ago.  And we finally did a week and a half ago.

Food was okay but unsure about charging 1500 baht for the famous crab omelette.  It was tasty, however, unsure if paying 1500 baht justified it.  Tasted other dishes too and felt the same. They were way overpriced for their taste and serving proportions.

Lastly, there were very minimal (to none) smiles which were evident on the staff's faces.  (No, it didn't appear uberly busy.  There was no line outside when we got there and plenty of tables available when we came.)  Service experienced from the staff was rather cold and quite abrupt, sadly. (That's the nicest and fairest way I can generally put it.)  After politely and honestly giving feedback to the lady who served us as we were about to leave, she apologised towards the end. (Giving credit where credit is due.)

Glad we ticked this off our food adventure list but not considering of going back if we are to travel back to BKK again.
sample_reviews_en.author: Jazen Eroles

sample_reviews_en.text:
Ja Fai is known for using premium-quality ingredients that are fresh, generously sized, and carefully selected. One thing I really enjoyed was the distinctive aroma from the charcoal-fired wok, which adds a wonderful smoky flavor to the dishes.
The food is consistently prepared and definitely tasty. However, as a Thai diner, I personally didn't find the flavors exceptionally outstanding or "mind-blowing." That said, the dishes are well-balanced and approachable, making them a great introduction to Thai cuisine for international visitors. Most tourists are likely to leave satisfied and impressed.
The prices are undeniably high, but considering the quality, freshness, and portion size of the ingredients, they are understandable. You're paying not only for the food itself but also for the premium ingredients and the unique cooking technique that has made Ja Fai famous. Overall, it's worth trying at least once, especially for visitors looking to experience one of Bangkok's most iconic street-food restaurants.
sample_reviews_en.author: Gargoyle Jibinoriko

sample_reviews_en.text:
Flew 20 hrs to eat Jay Fai’s cooking!!!

Didn’t disappoint. We’re from Washington DC/Maryland USA, where we KNOW crabs!!! This crab omelette is perfection…why? Because she lets the lump crab meat be the star of the show. No extra seasoning, no filler, just a nice thin crunchy coating on the outside.

Dish #2 - Dry Tom Yum - just order it! All of the flavor of an incredible soup without the broth. Shrimp are enormous and enough to share for two.

Dish #3 - Drunken Noodle - again, just order it already!!!! Flavors are amazing and so fresh! Massive prawns and not overcooked.

Husband and I shared three and we were stuffed but not sick. Worth EVERY penny!!! You pay a premium for excellence. 🥰

Can’t take a photo with Jay Fai, but I got a photo with her daughter, who was just a kind and amazing.

Thank you Mrs Fai for all your talents and years of feeding us your food. So so happy we got to experience your art before retiring. 🙏🏼
sample_reviews_en.author: D. Johnson

sample_reviews_en.text:
Jay Fai: Huge Portions, Fresh Seafood, Worth Every Baht! 🦀🔥
The hype is real. The ingredients are massive, ultra-fresh, and completely justify the price. Every dish was a hit!
The Highlights:
Crab Omelet: A total must-try. Paired with her signature chili sauce, it’s mind-blowingly delicious.
Abalone with Chinese Broccoli: Pure, honest flavor. So good we ordered a second plate!
Stir-fried Coconut Shoots with Prawns: My new second-favorite dish. We literally refused to let them clear the plate just so we could mix the remaining sauce with rice!
Seafood Khua Gai: Jay Fai’s daughter worried we’d get "seafood fatigue" and suggested chicken. Our reply? "At Jay Fai, it’s seafood or nothing!"
Also loved: The smoky Pad Kee Mao, Rich Dry Seafood Congee, and the aromatic Garlic Fried Seafood.
Verdict: Zero regrets. Massive sizes, incredible flavor, and completely worth the money!
sample_reviews_en.author: Sirisorn Popradit

sample_reviews_en.text:
Jay Fai’s crab omelette is a real must-try! For 1,500 baht, we thnk it is well worth it. It’s 95% filled with plump and juicy crab meat. (We actually tried crab omelette in another restaurant for 1,200 baht and it was practically just omelette with very few pieces of crab meat). We loved Jay Fai’s crab omelette so much that we ordered a second one.

Go after lunch to avoid the long queue. We went at around 2:30pm on a Thursday and got a table right away.

We also didn’t experience any of the negative reviews we read about in Google. The staff, including Jay Fai’s daughter, were efficient and polite. The place was also clean, especially the toilet.

It’s understandable that they don’t allow any photos with Jay Fai. Because if each and every customer will ask for a photo, then she will not be able to cook anymore. 😅

Overall, we highly recommend visiting Jay Fai.❤️
sample_reviews_en.author: Rio Ilao

restaurants.name: O-Jung Premium รัชดา 18
restaurants.address:

243 275 Ratchadaphisek Rd, Ratchadaphisek, Din Daeng, Bangkok 10310, Thailand
restaurants.price_level: Photo of reviewer who wrote "The vegetables are very overpriced and served in small portions."

sample_reviews_en.text:
I dined here on September 29, 2024, from approximately 7:40 PM to 9:40 PM.
I was alone and the bill was over 1700 baht. This was my fourth time dining here, but this time I was very disappointed. The staff were very rushed, almost like they were indirectly trying to get me to leave. Around 9:30 PM, the staff kept clearing the plates, over and over again, to the point where it felt like they were rushing me out because it was almost closing time. In the end, there were absolutely no plates, chopsticks, or bowls left on my table – not even empty plates. It was like they were trying to make it clear to the customer that closing time was approaching. I felt terrible because I was almost finished eating. I gave them a 100 baht tip and told them not to come back at night or late at night.

I usually go around 8 PM and leave around 9:30 PM. I'm definitely not going back here again.

What kind of restaurant would have you experience where, close to closing time, the staff rushes to clear your table, and then three people stand beside you, seemingly pressuring you to leave because it's almost closing time and you're the last 2-3 tables?
sample_reviews_en.author: Enson wang

sample_reviews_en.text:
I arrived around 1 PM and the restaurant was empty, with only a few tables occupied. The parking lot was spacious and convenient. The staff were attentive, constantly changing the grill grate for me.
The food selection, especially the meat, was reasonably priced. The prices weren't too high, around 1000 baht per plate, making it comparable to other restaurants. You'd have to order Wagyu beef, which costs 1000+ baht per plate, to really jump in price. It's not much different from the expensive restaurants in Thonglor (it might even be more expensive for some dishes). Personally, I prefer the salt-marinated Kurobuta pork here. As for the bacon, to make it different from sliced ​​pork belly, they should switch to thicker slices for a better texture and to pair perfectly with the garlic fried rice.
sample_reviews_en.author: OHM

sample_reviews_en.text: The meat quality was substandard. The first dish was delicious, but the second was terrible; a completely different experience. When I asked the staff member who served me, they didn't come over to check the meat at my table. They just replied from afar that they hadn't served the wrong meat and asked me to check if the two dishes were the same. (They replied that they were slightly different, but not slightly! And I ordered Arakat, so all the dishes should have been equally good.) The difference was in the toughness, not in the marbling.
sample_reviews_en.author: PS BT

sample_reviews_en.text:
This restaurant has ample parking.
The food is grilled.
The vegetables are very fresh and crispy; the salad is delicious even if you're eating it alone.
It's good value for money. If you like beef with marbling, you should try it.

After your meal, you can choose one dessert per person. Fruit is served after you finish your meal, so you don't need to get up.
If you come in the evening around 7 PM, it's not usually crowded. The tables are large, so you don't have to worry if you're coming with a large group.
sample_reviews_en.author: Neyney Natthapailin

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a restaurant you really have to go to for the premium-grade grilled meat because the menu only has meat, salad, and fried rice.
We arrived at Ban Mong, there were only two tables occupied, and the food was very slow. Several staff members were in a meeting, but only one person got up to serve. It seemed like there was only one person in the kitchen as well. Even ordering a salad took a long time.
We hadn't even finished eating and the bill was over 2000 baht.
sample_reviews_en.author: Diane Namchai

sample_reviews_en.text:
One of the long established yakiniku restaurants, offering a wide variety of proteins with quality that matches the price.

The dipping sauces are well-suited to Thai tastes.

The vegetables are very overpriced and served in small portions.

Service is fairly standard. The restaurant is quite old, but it has been continuously maintained and renovated, so it remains clean and not run down.
sample_reviews_en.author: Krittayot Chaowanapreecha

sample_reviews_en.text:
This restaurant is perfect for meat lovers, offering many grades of high-quality, tender, and delicious meat.

The service was good and polite, but there were slight delays, possibly due to a large number of customers arriving at the same time.

The prices are quite high; a plate of the meat shown in the picture costs 2,000-2,500 THB, not including 7% VAT and 10% service charge.
sample_reviews_en.author: GongGang

sample_reviews_en.text: I used the parking service in the morning, checking in at 9:58 AM and checking out at 11:17 AM. The total should have been 40 baht, but the staff said it was 50 baht, citing a sign at the Land Department office saying 20 baht per hour. If that's the shop's policy of charging a flat rate, I understand, but if not, please observe the staff's behavior. Thank you.
sample_reviews_en.author: TONE NEUNG

restaurants.name: Bang Phai Thong
restaurants.address:

32 Phet Kasem 25/2 Alley, Pak Khlong Phasi Charoen, Phasi Charoen, Bangkok 10160, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a Hainanese chicken rice restaurant I frequent because it's delicious, but the taste varies somewhat each time.

1. Before - the soup had a fragrant pickled lime flavor with a slight sourness. / Most recently - the aroma is very faint, almost as if it wasn't added at all, and the sourness is gone.

2. Before - the rice was soft, fragrant, and oily. / Most recently - the rice was hard, like it wasn't cooked properly.

3. Before - the chicken was delicious and tender. / Most recently - some parts of the meat were cold, tough, and had an off smell.

The only thing that always tastes the same is the dipping sauce.
Tea isn't free; it's probably 2 baht per glass (I didn't order tea the last time).
The service is average; I haven't encountered any problems yet.

The price is reasonable, and the portion size is commensurate with the price.
sample_reviews_en.author: Oomchu Pichit

sample_reviews_en.text:
I've actually been eating here for twenty years, since I was a kid.
I moved to work in another province and only got to try it a few times, but I don't know if anyone else feels the same way, but lately the rice has been very soggy and not as fragrant as before. Before, I considered their rice the best; even the plain rice was edible. Now I don't like it at all. The rice grains aren't whole, they seem broken. I don't know if they're using bad quality rice or if it's just not cooked properly. It's a real shame. But the boiled chicken is still as tender as ever.
sample_reviews_en.author: BS

sample_reviews_en.text:
I ordered chicken with skin and meat, but when it arrived, there was no skin. This shows a lack of attention to detail and I'm deducting points for the service. As for the taste, it was just average. The rice was soft but not fragrant and almost tasteless. The chicken wasn't very tender, probably suitable for those who like to chew. The dipping sauce was also just a basic one, without any chili or garlic provided.
Overall, it was mediocre. You can find similar food anywhere; there's no need to specifically go out of your way to eat here.
sample_reviews_en.author: dove phawin

sample_reviews_en.text: This chicken rice shop really brings back childhood memories — from the nostalgic look of the place to the familiar flavors, especially the soup made with pickled lime. They even have a special chili-ginger mix to blend with their signature chicken rice sauce, which is quite unique. The dark soy sauce here is more on the bitter side, though I personally prefer it sweeter. Plus, the owner is so friendly and welcome. Overall, I think it’s definitely worth a try.
sample_reviews_en.author: Gunn Nimmans

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is the most fragrant rice I've ever eaten in Hainanese chicken rice.
The rice grains are fluffy, fragrant, and perfectly oily. Served with the chicken dipping sauce, which has finely chopped chili, garlic, and ginger, it's the best!!
The chicken is on the drier side, but not tough or dry.
Overall, it's delicious. If you're in the area, I highly recommend trying it.

The price is reasonable and matches the quality 👍🏻✨
sample_reviews_en.author: Apichaya M.

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is my absolute favorite Hainanese chicken rice shop. It's the most delicious and perfect for my taste.
The chicken is tender and tasty, the rice is beautifully cooked and soft, the dipping sauce is fragrant and delicious with chopped chili and ginger, and the soup is made with pickled lime – simply amazing. I'm incredibly impressed with the taste! I've been eating here since kindergarten until now that I'm working.
sample_reviews_en.author: Benjawan Jirasakmongkol

sample_reviews_en.text: They don't sell plain rice with toppings. If you want rice with toppings, not just minced chicken as a dish, the restaurant won't sell you rice. I ordered a special, and when I asked to buy extra rice, they wouldn't sell it to me. These are just my personal opinions; I personally don't like it, and I won't argue that everything else is delicious—the chicken is good, the rice is good.
sample_reviews_en.author: Rowan Allen

sample_reviews_en.text: This is my favorite restaurant. I eat here all the time. The rice is fragrant, delicious, and fluffy. The chicken is chewy, the thigh meat is flavorful, and the liver is tender. The pickled lime soup is the highlight! Parking is available at the gas station next door.
sample_reviews_en.author: Los sentimientos

restaurants.name: Wilai
restaurants.address:

288 Charoen Krung 53 Alley, Khwaeng Yan Nawa, Khet Sathon, Bangkok 10120, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text:
Dry noodles with red pork wontons and a rich gravy. Delicious! Regular is 50฿, special is 60฿. A satisfying meal for those who like to eat a lot or who want to bring breakfast along.
But if you're not too hungry, the regular is just the right amount of filling. Seating is in the alley across from the restaurant.
sample_reviews_th.author: YONG MAHANAM

sample_reviews_en.text:
The bamee is so delicious, seasoning oil is so fragrant, lots of chubby wontons and BBQ pork slices and sprinkled with fried pork lard. Yummy.
A lovely Myanmar lady serve us nicely, greeting and smiling, respond to us patiently. Very convenience.
Dine-in area across the street, cool and breezy.
At 50 baht for a big bowl bamee with that lots of toppings is definitely cheap.
Highly recommended.
sample_reviews_en.author: Rbw dinata

sample_reviews_en.text: The taste is terrible, absolutely awful. I've had much better before. I don't know how they're trying to make a profit. They're asking for sympathy for the vendor, but please be considerate of the consumer too. Doing business like this, they'll never have any customers. It's a shame about how delicious it used to be. 😤😮‍💨😮‍💨😮‍💨🙄🙄🙄 Anyone thinking of buying, think again. I don't recommend it.
sample_reviews_en.author: สุพัตรา ดํารงเกียรติดี

sample_reviews_en.text: The portion size is very generous, overflowing the bowl. The noodles are perfectly cooked, springy and not starchy, but they're very oily. This might be good for those who like soggy noodles. The pork dumplings are tasty and don't contain a …
sample_reviews_en.author: Peter Lai

sample_reviews_en.text: It was the most delicious food I had in Bangkok....!! I didn't originally want to write a review, but I wanted to keep it to myself, so I hope everyone tries it once...!!! It's really delicious!!! And it only costs 50 baht per bowl.!!!!!
sample_reviews_en.author: 유수

sample_reviews_en.text: I've been eating this since I was a kid. Today I went back and bought some again, and the taste is still as delicious as ever. Before, I used to eat in the shop, but now they have seating in the alley across the street. The last time I …
sample_reviews_en.author: Abple Chis

sample_reviews_en.text: They give generous portions of sauce that's slightly sweet. The special order comes with 5 large dumplings. The soup is easy to drink. There's no parking lot; even motorcycles have difficulty parking, but there are some spots available.
sample_reviews_en.author: ck 2509

sample_reviews_en.text: The noodles are chewy and soft, the dumplings are delicious, and the roast pork is just the right amount of flavor. You can eat it without seasoning to get the same delicious taste without being too oily. The soup is easy to swallow.
sample_reviews_en.author: Natakhon Mongkhon

restaurants.name: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวคั่วไก่ นายตรี ราชพฤกษ์
restaurants.address:

7/51 Bang Chueak Nang, Taling Chan, Bangkok 10170, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
Charcoal-Grilled Stir-Fried Chicken Restaurant, a must-try in Ratchaphruek.
Each dish is stir-fried to order, delicious and reasonably priced.
Besides the stir-fried chicken, the pork bone soup with pickled lime is also excellent.

Crispy Stir-Fried Mixed Ingredients:
: Chicken, ham, shrimp, crispy squid.
: If you order the crispy stir-fried version, they will crack an egg
and fry it with the noodles until crispy.
It's fried to a perfect dry and crispy texture
because they drain the oil before serving.

Baked Stir-Fried Chicken Only:
: If you order the baked version, the noodles are fried until crispy,
then an egg is cracked and placed on top, baked until the outside of the egg is cooked.

Pork Bone Soup with Pickled Lime:
: Another highlight.
The restaurant uses pork bones with meat attached.
The soup is fragrant with pickled lime, perfect for cutting through the richness.

Besides stir-fried chicken,
they also have many other à la carte dishes and snacks.
Prices start at just 40 baht.
Air-conditioned seating is also available.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nuch Chava

sample_reviews_en.text:
I liked it and will probably visit again.
I clicked on the map and ran, almost missed the shop because the sign was quite hard to see, and I couldn't see any tables. I thought the shop was closed. Turns out, there's an air-conditioned seating area inside with a TV.
I ordered the stir-fried noodles with chicken. The noodles were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, but a bit bland (like they weren't seasoned). You have to eat it with the well-marinated chicken and chili sauce, and it's delicious. So I ordered two boxes to take home. I ate them all myself. They were good, but not as delicious as eating at the shop because the parts that should be crispy were too soft. But the taste was still good.
I'll go back and try the takeout next time I'm in the area.
sample_reviews_en.author: Kitipat Rerkrai

sample_reviews_en.text: This is Chinese-style stir-fried chicken noodles. The flavor isn't too strong, and it lacks the typical wok-fried aroma; it's more about the homemade seasoning. The noodle texture is good, and the ingredients are high quality, but it can get a bit greasy after a while because the noodles are deep-fried. If you prefer stir-fried chicken noodles that are pre-seasoned, have a fragrant wok-fried aroma, and have soft, slightly burnt noodles, this place might not be for you. However, they provide a pickled lemon soup to cut through the greasiness. As for the regular noodles, we thought they were just average. You can park in front of the shop along the street.
sample_reviews_en.author: Maie Chubbie

sample_reviews_en.text:
"Khao Kai Nai Tree, a roadside noodle shop on Ratchaphruek Road, near Suan Mali."
Located right by the roadside on the inbound side of Ratchaphruek Road, you'll need to look carefully. Khao Kai Nai Tree is a small roadside noodle shop specializing in stir-fried and baked noodles. The baked noodles include an egg with a runny yolk. The noodles are crispy on the outside but may not be heavily seasoned. The chicken is served in large, tender, and delicious pieces. In addition, the shop also offers other dishes like flavorful basil chicken rice and tasty snacks such as fried chicken wings.
The shop is open from 11:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
sample_reviews_en.author: Art Suwarnatemiya

sample_reviews_en.text:
"Nai Tree's" stir-fried chicken noodles is an old, established shop run by the older brother of the owner of "Ann's Stir-fried Chicken," a famous shop in the Suan Mali area. "Nai Tree" has been helping to make stir-fried chicken noodles at "Ann's Stir-fried Chicken" since before the shop became well-known.

Please come and try it! Personally, I think it's even tastier than the Suan Mali shop.
sample_reviews_en.author: กันย์ สินธุประเสริฐ

sample_reviews_en.text: Rajapruek's signature stir-fried chicken offers both baked and stir-fried options, with a delicious pickled lime soup. They used to sell rice, but now they do. Their crispy pork basil stir-fry is just as good as the stir-fried chicken. They also have snacks like fish cakes, fried chicken, and crispy chicken skin. The prices are reasonable, the service is fast, and they have air conditioning.
sample_reviews_en.author: Bestlingchan

sample_reviews_en.text: The fried noodles are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. They're already delicious even when eaten hot without sauce. The chicken is tender, the squid is crispy, and the shrimp are fresh. The price is 60-70 baht, very worthwhile. What's great is that the fried noodles are very good, not greasy at all. However, the shop is quite small, not very inviting to sit in.
sample_reviews_en.author: Knight D

sample_reviews_en.text: Stir-fried chicken and squid 60.- The noodles have a crispy outer crust and are soft on the inside, but lack the fragrant wok-fried aroma. The chicken is slightly salty, and the squid pieces are large and bouncy. Overall, the flavors blend well. The restaurant has air conditioning and accepts QR code payments. Parking is available along the roadside.
sample_reviews_en.author: Suprinya Pan

restaurants.name: IKKYU Yakinikudokoro
restaurants.address:

40 soi Thonglor 13 Sukhumvit 49 RD Klongton-Nua Wattana, Khlong Tan, เหนือ, Bangkok 10110, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text: If you are looking for top-quality Yakiniku, this place is a must-visit! The beef quality is outstanding—beautiful marbling, incredibly tender, and packed with flavor. The soy-based tare marinade strikes the perfect balance of savory and sweet without overpowering the natural taste of the meat. Everything from the fresh veggies to the side garnishes was beautifully presented. Service was fast, attentive, and helpful with the grill. 10/10 experience, will definitely be coming back!
sample_reviews_en.author: Fahkhram Boutique

sample_reviews_en.text:
Came here twice already.

Reasonable price for the quality of the meat. The wagyu here is high quality and they serve with tasty sauce. Large variety of menus; they offer both large and small sets of beef, chicken, pork of various qualities.

Recommend for both people who are looking for high quality wagyu yakiniku or someone who looks for a tasty casual affordable meal.

Overall service is good, the staffs are attentive. This place has became my favorite yakiniku restaurant.
sample_reviews_en.author: Tanisa L.

sample_reviews_en.text: Wagyu and Kobe beef very reasonably priced. The sets were of great value and they offered a lot of discounts. Melts in your mouth. Their vegetables were also fresh and pairs well with the meat. The location is of the restaurant is subtle, but that’s what makes it feel like a hidden gem. One thing that the restaurant could improve on would be installing some kind of smoke system at the grill so that smoke isn’t everywhere while guests eat.
sample_reviews_en.author: Proddy Sukcharoen

sample_reviews_en.text:
- Lunch set menu and promotion posted in front of the restaurant during the weekend but the staff said this is the promotion for weekday only !?!!?
- The food here is very expensive
- The staff are so hard to find.. they are not around where you can see them easily
- The meat is ok, some of them are not really tender as expected from the price
sample_reviews_en.author: Duangkamol L.

sample_reviews_en.text: This place is a must-visit. The quality is very good for the price. every single cut was incredibly tender, juicy, and literally melted in my mouth. The charcoal grill added a perfect smoky aroma to the meat. Service was fast and attentive. It is worth every single penny. I will definitely come back!
sample_reviews_en.author: Suttida Krataitong

sample_reviews_en.text: This place takes me back to my days eating at Daidomon Yakiniku as a kid. No fuss vibe of grilling your own meat at the table. The cuts are quality, the sauce is spot on. There are many cuts we want to try that make us want to keep ordering. Definitely coming back.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
sample_reviews_en.author: Tanakrit

sample_reviews_en.text:
✨Highly recommend ✨
The meat here is amazingly good. I’ve been coming here for quite some time now, and the taste is still exceptionally great. The staff here are friendly and provide excellent service. For those who travel here by car, there is also a parking lot available.
sample_reviews_en.author: Boonchuay Okabe

sample_reviews_en.text:
On the busy Thonglor Soi 13 and in a quiet alley.
Superb yakiniku (grilled meat) and lunch set is very surprisingly affordable. Meat was tender and fresh. Service efficient and had the feel on a Japanese small eatery. 5 star diner. Very good for lunch and quick Dinner
sample_reviews_en.author: Simon Tang

restaurants.name: Aoi Siam Paragon
restaurants.address:

991 Rama I Rd, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330, Thailand
restaurants.price_level: Photo of reviewer who wrote "Small portions totally overpriced from the menu recommended by the waitress."

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is one of our favorite Japanese restaurants in Bangkok, and a place we have happily returned to many times over the years. Surprisingly, despite being regular guests, we had never written a review—so it is definitely time to share our experience.

The quality of the ingredients is consistently outstanding, and every dish is prepared with great care and precision. The sushi is exceptionally fresh, with each piece practically melting in your mouth. The grilled fish, especially the snow fish and the salmon topped with shrimp roe, is perfectly cooked and full of flavor. Even the garlic fried rice, although seemingly simple, is incredibly satisfying and surprisingly addictive. The spicy tuna maki is another standout that we always enjoy. Una ju is also my favorite dish.

To be honest, we have yet to find a dish that disappoints us. Every meal has been consistently delicious, which is why we keep coming back.

The service is also efficient.

Overall, AOI continues to be one of our top choices for authentic Japanese cuisine in Bangkok. With its exceptional food, consistent quality, and nice ambiance , it is a restaurant we highly recommend and will certainly continue to visit.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nutharin Phusitphoykai

sample_reviews_en.text:
This place is always our to-go place for celebrating life events. It sits inside Siam Paragon so it’s super easy to visit and offers great quality Japanese meal. If it was a rainy day, or after work celebration, or didn’t want to walk in a deep Bangkok’s alley to get great Japanese restaurant, Aoi always got you.

Even visiting it many times, we’ve never ordered the same menus. This time we ordered Ankimo, lunch set of grilled Sanma with shoyu on rice and MAI lunch set. They were such a roller coaster of taste.

We start off with bowl of creamy Ankimo. Not the best Ankimo in our life but definitely one of the high quality one. It served with ponzu and spicy grated radish. For the grilled Sanma, this dish surprised me. The smell was just like Unaju with Kabayaki sauce but here is Sanma where it can only be found during late summer and autumn. Then came the grand presentation of MAI set that start off with small glass of sweet liquor and followed by variety of small seafood dishes served. Good looking appetizers, fried dish, grilled dish and fresh sashimi.

We were fall for it and will definitely consider ordering this set again for our next visit.
sample_reviews_en.author: Mindodoo

sample_reviews_en.text: This was a pretty disappointing experience. We spent around 2000 baht per person for various food which was okay but not special for this price, thus 3 stars. For a restaurant in this price range, however, I would expect some kind of service which was non-existent. 1. We were not greeted when we came in 2. orders were not taken accurately 3. servers stared at us all the time 4. nobody smiled at any time which is quite unusual for Thailand 5. every additional service has to be paid extra, even for plain water I was charged. At no time did we have the feeling that we were welcome. The atmosphere is subpar. It looks nice from the outside, but inside the chairs and tables are stacked closely to each other that is unworthy of a restaurant with ambitions to serve an affluent clientele. I definitely do not recommend wasting your money here.
sample_reviews_en.author: C L

sample_reviews_en.text:
My friends and I have always made it a point to visit Aoi@Siam Paragon for nice Japanese food our every BKK holiday. Over the years, Aoi has managed to attract and maintain a steady flow of Japanese cuisine food aficionados.
We ordered 3 sets: a shokadou yuki, a misokatsu (breaded deep-fried pork cutlet) and a sake saba-fish. They came accompanied nicely with rice and a dessert (yuzu jelly or ice-cream scoop).
We enjoyed the food very much: totally delish and wonderful!
The restaurant ambience was serene and quiet, conducive for enjoying a quiet meal at own pace.
Staff were attentive but without fussing around tables, and they provided meticulous service to customers.
sample_reviews_en.author: Sim Simon

sample_reviews_en.text:
My cousin brought us here for dinner. The decor and design of the restaurant is great. It has a proper Japanese feel to it. Even the staff wore kimonos.

The food was ordinary, especially considering the price. I had been expecting something to shine but everything ended up being somewhat average. They used high quality ingredients, sure, but the taste wasn't memorable.

The bento had an absolutely brilliant presentation though. It came in a two tiered box and in little plates. Really loved that!

Overall, the experience was good for the service, environment, and presentation.
sample_reviews_en.author: Don L

sample_reviews_en.text:
Aoi may not be the fanciest or most upscale Japanese restaurant in Paragon Mall, but it certainly is one of the best. Its food menu is extensive, offering sushi, sashimi, tempura, ramen, teppanyaki, donburi, udon, and more.

The restaurant also offers a variety of set meal options, which make it a great budget-friendly option for those looking to experience some authentic Japanese cuisine without breaking the bank. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting and the service is friendly and attentive.

All in all, Aoi is a great option for a delicious and reasonably priced meal.
sample_reviews_en.author: Wisanu Tuntawiroon

sample_reviews_en.text: I must have walked past this place a hundred times without giving it a second thought. It always looked nice, but for some reason, I never felt the urge to go in. Then one day, on a whim, I decided to give it a try—and I’m so glad I did. The set menu was surprisingly thoughtful and balanced, with each dish tasting fresh and carefully prepared. The tea was fragrant and comforting, the kind that makes you slow down and enjoy the moment. It instantly felt like a hidden gem I had overlooked for too long. Now, every time I find myself at Paragon, this is my go-to spot.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pepper Porodina

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a Japanese restaurant located on the first floor (G floor) of the Siam Paragon department store, slightly past Starbucks, Kasikorn Bank, and Talling Pling.

I believe it's a sister restaurant to the one in Emporium.

Honestly, the prices are a little on the higher side, but the taste and service are excellent, making it a reliable and trustworthy restaurant.

My parents, who were visiting from Japan, were delighted and very impressed by the delicious food and the service, including the complimentary tea, which felt just like in Japan.

Thank you! 😋
sample_reviews_en.author: moko Kiri

restaurants.name: ซุปเปอร์มัง
restaurants.address:

45, 129 Sukhonthasawat Rd, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text: This was my first time at this restaurant. My boyfriend recommended it, saying the food was good. Most of the reviews said it was delicious, so we went with four people and ordered five dishes. It was all delicious; the taste was great and it was more than worth the price. The atmosphere was like a typical restaurant, with some background noise, which is normal. There was live music in the evenings, and before that, they played background music. The total bill was 600฿, which is about 150฿ per person – very affordable considering they even had crab omelet! Overall, I liked it. If you're interested, I recommend giving this restaurant a try.
sample_reviews_th.author: Warittaya

sample_reviews_en.text:
A roadside rice porridge stall, but the taste is extraordinary.

Inexpensive rice porridge stall with plenty of parking. Clean shop, accepts cash and bank transfers. Plenty of tables, food arrives quickly, and lots of staff.

The food is flavorful and delicious, comparable to famous restaurants.
The portion sizes are very reasonable for the price.

Dishes I tried:

- ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Stir-fried clams with basil: Perfectly sized clams, well-balanced flavor, fragrant basil. Great with rice or rice porridge, not greasy. A nice change from the usual chili paste stir-fries with milk.

- Spicy soup: Flavorful and easy to drink.
- Stir-fried sunflower sprouts: Very flavorful.
- Stir-fried shrimp claws with chili and salt: Dry, good as a snack or with rice or rice porridge.

The menu is extensive, tables are readily available, and there's a constant flow of customers. Plenty of parking in the market. The shop is located in the market, right on the road. 👍👍👍👍
sample_reviews_en.author: S Chan

sample_reviews_en.text:
This famous rice porridge shop is near Satri Witthaya 2 School.
The food tastes great, with rich, flavorful broth perfect to eat with rice porridge, or even without it. The stir-fried clams here use large clams that don't shrink after frying; just mixing the broth with rice is delicious! 😆
The stir-fried pork with preserved olives uses high-quality minced pork with a little fat, topped with fragrant fried garlic, and stir-fried to a savory and delicious flavor. The spicy salad with salted fish has a perfect balance of sour, sweet, salty, and spicy. Even simple dishes like stir-fried kale with salted fish are very fragrant with the salted fish, and the kale is perfectly crispy, not too hard or too soft. The rice porridge here is nice and thick; some places only have a little bit of rice water. 😅 Importantly, everything is reasonably priced, making it a comfortable place for a late-night meal.
sample_reviews_en.author: Mommam Progressive

sample_reviews_en.text:
The quantity and taste are contradictory!?
We ordered a lot, but the bill was surprisingly cheap. We loved it! The rice porridge was delicious on its own, and with coconut milk and sticky rice it was even better. The sea bass with mussels is hard to find, so we ordered two plates.
This is my second visit because I was persuaded by a friend who dragged me here. I usually don't eat dinner, but I was willing to pay because this place is open at 5 pm. The steamed rice cakes were so delicious we had to fight other tables for them. I wouldn't deduct stars if it had air conditioning, but if it did, we probably wouldn't be able to eat at this price. 😊
sample_reviews_en.author: Prapas Ton

sample_reviews_en.text: This roadside rice porridge restaurant has plenty of parking, so no worries there. It's one of the places highly recommended by locals. The stir-fried morning glory with crispy pork is delicious. It seems their stir-fried dishes are their specialty. The pork slices are thin and crispy, fried until dry. The tom yum soup is flavorful and rich. The omelet is plain. The rice porridge is served in a unique butterfly pea flower color. The bowl isn't very big; the portion feels a bit small. The prices are typical for a rice porridge restaurant.
sample_reviews_en.author: Jeffey

sample_reviews_en.text:
When I think of a good rice porridge restaurant, I always recommend this place. The food tastes familiar, and they have some dishes that are hard to find elsewhere, such as sour curry with Ryukyu fish roe and sweet fried fish slices, etc.
I've been many times and have never been disappointed. One day, there was someone singing and playing guitar, which was amazing. I even bought some to take home for my family.
And the rice porridge itself is very fragrant and easy to drink.
sample_reviews_en.author: Aun Chino

sample_reviews_en.text:
I eat here very often, especially late at night. I often stop by to buy food to take home (the picture shows spicy beef tendon soup). There's plenty of parking and the food comes out quickly ✨✨ My frequently ordered dishes are:
- Spicy beef tendon soup
- Braised duck intestines
- Crispy pork/stir-fried tofu with chili and salt
- Fried cabbage with fish sauce
- Fried chicken tendons
- Stir-fried squid with salted egg
sample_reviews_en.author: wanderer

sample_reviews_en.text:
Rice porridge and side dish stall in the market / Plenty of seating with various seating areas.
- Stir-fried tofu with chili and salt: Crispy and delicious.
- Stir-fried crispy pork with chili and salt: Well-fried.
- Spicy sausage and dried fish salad: Very well-balanced flavor. ⭐️
- Creamy tom yum soup with shrimp: Perfectly balanced sweet and sour.
- Crispy fried duck intestines: Great as a snack.
sample_reviews_en.author: JANG Pogus

restaurants.name: SUNDAE ice-cream Cafe & Brunch
restaurants.address:

1st floor, 20/2 Phraeng Sanphasat Rd, San Chao Pho Sua, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
I found this place by chance. I was passing by the Chao Pho Suea shrine and it was so hot, so I stopped to find an air-conditioned place to get some cold drinks. I stumbled upon this shop and stopped in without expecting much. The atmosphere was amazing – great vibe, cool air conditioning, and a really cool theme. They make homemade ice cream, and it's incredibly delicious with the corn. The coffee is good too. A real hidden gem!

This was my second visit. The shop has moved slightly from its original location.
The mood has changed a bit, but the shop is still very cute. The ice cream is just as delicious as before.
sample_reviews_en.author: ทนายโบ วารุณี

sample_reviews_en.text: Very friendly service—the lady speaks English well and had no problem letting me charge my phone during the visit, for which I’m grateful. The ice cream was also excellent and very tasty. She even let me sample the flavors before choosing, which was really nice. The place seems renovated and has a great vibe. I’ll definitely come back for another scoop on my next visit to Bangkok!
sample_reviews_en.author: Grzegorz Zielinski

sample_reviews_en.text:
The homemade ice cream is amazing! I especially loved the strawberry yogurt ice cream; it paired perfectly with the toast. The toast was incredibly delicious! 😋😋🤎🍧 I think everything on the menu is worth trying.
The owner is lovely, and I also saw Jannimit Cider. I'll definitely stop by again when I have the chance! 🤍
sample_reviews_en.author: Maneerut N.

sample_reviews_en.text: The ice cream is so delicious! 😋 The shop is cute and has a great atmosphere. There's a cozy sofa area to relax on, and a craft beer fridge to choose from 🍺. I'm impressed and will definitely stop by often whenever I have the chance. P.S. The owner is so lovely and let me sample every flavor in the fridge! 🍦
sample_reviews_en.author: Na P.

sample_reviews_en.text:
Great coffee, homemade cake, super friendly people.

Great coffee can be hard to find in Thailand. This place has it plus all the extra you hope to find like friendly staff and home made cake (you can taste the love). If you’re in the neighbourhood make a visit and experience it for yourself.
sample_reviews_en.author: arjanbeerman

sample_reviews_en.text:
Orange Americano: 110 baht
The orange juice wasn't quite to my liking, but the coffee was fragrant.
You can bring your own cup! ✨✨🌳

The atmosphere is nice, they have board games, perfect for chilling out. There's a wide selection of menu items.

The shop is open from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pannipa K

sample_reviews_en.text:
Good food, good mood.

The scones were delicious! The buttery aroma was wonderful, and the strawberry jam was amazing!

The Suwannaphum pineapple ice cream was the best!
The Pipo yogurt ice cream was fantastic!
The rum raisin ice cream was fragrant and delicious.

Highly recommended!
sample_reviews_en.author: Wanyupon Pansuk

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a cute shop with a great atmosphere. There's an indoor area with air conditioning – perfect after a hot day! Delicious ice cream awaits. There's also an outdoor area with some stylish photo opportunities.

The pineapple sorbet is amazing, and the peach yogurt is also good.
sample_reviews_en.author: Man Thirawat

restaurants.name: กิมง้วนลูกชิ้นปลา สาขาพระราม5 - นครอินทร์
restaurants.address:

22 Nakhon In Rd, Bang Khun Kong, Bang Kruai District, Nonthaburi 11130, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text: Kim Ng้วน Fishball Restaurant has several branches. Their fishballs are delicious. This branch is located past the Rama 5 Market and next to Pornprasert Secondhand Goods. They have many recommended menu items. I ordered the regular Yentafo noodles (69 baht, 89 baht with toppings). The taste was good, rich, with a tangy and spicy kick. They gave a generous portion of noodles, and the crispy squid wasn't chewy. I also ordered the Tom Yum Goong (spicy noodle soup), regular (69 baht, 89 baht with toppings). I liked this dish; the thin noodles were well-seasoned and flavorful. The fishballs were good quality, with a sign displaying award certificates for several years (including Michelin). The restaurant doesn't have air conditioning, but there is parking available.
sample_reviews_th.author: Ph031

sample_reviews_th.text:
Kim Ng้วน Fishball Restaurant, a famous restaurant that has received Michelin awards for many years, has several branches.

We ordered the Tom Yum Fishball Hot Pot with Egg (L size). It was served looking very appetizing. The flavor was rich, a little too sweet (to my personal preference), so I asked for more lime juice/spicy dressing to add. The taste was perfect and suited our palate.

The boiled seafood platter was tasty and had a decent amount of ingredients.

There is free parking in front of the restaurant.
sample_reviews_th.author: Pimthada Sahachatiraklap

sample_reviews_en.text: This restaurant has been Michelin-starred for 5 consecutive years, and it lives up to its reputation for deliciousness. The prices are reasonable. Fish ball lovers absolutely must try it because it's truly amazing. The fish noodles are good, the fish dumplings are excellent, and the tom yum soup is perfectly balanced even if you don't like it too spicy. My recommended dish is the tom yum fish noodle soup. It's a bit pricey, but it includes seaweed fish balls, which aren't usually on the regular menu, and you get to try all the different types of fish balls available. The atmosphere might be like a typical noodle shop, but the deliciousness makes you forget the location. It's located in a Japanese second-hand warehouse, so you can take a walk after your meal. This is my 4th or 5th visit, I can't remember exactly, but personally, I consider it the best fish balls I've ever had. I recommend ordering every dish with extra toppings for a truly satisfying experience.
sample_reviews_en.author: Narong Lumdee

sample_reviews_en.text:
Today's review is to commend the staff for their excellent and incredibly patient service. They didn't show any sign of displeasure when a customer didn't receive their order and refused to pay, even though they had already eaten some of the food. Even though the staff informed them that some items were out of stock, from a customer's perspective—first time at the restaurant—if we had already consumed some food and drinks, we would still pay for what we had eaten. The staff handled the situation very well. I don't want the owner to deduct any money or punish the staff in any way.
Regarding the food, it was fresh, delicious, and flavorful, with prices commensurate with the portion size. The meatballs were bouncy and chewy. They had run out of pork, but they informed us beforehand and replaced it with meatballs. The restaurant atmosphere is ordinary, and parking is limited, with about 7-8 spaces available on the street.
sample_reviews_en.author: Parichat S.

sample_reviews_en.text:
The highlight is the Yen Ta Fo (Thai noodle soup) with a sweet flavor profile, not sour, and without the strong fermented tofu smell. Delicious without needing any extra seasoning.
The meatballs are high-quality, fresh, and delicious. The squid is crispy and plentiful with a firm, crunchy texture.
The Tom Yum soup is clear with fresh lime, well-balanced, and the minced pork is tasty, not tough, and not too fatty.
The fried fish skin is delicious, but there's a little too little of it.

The dry noodles are chewy, soft, fragrant, and perfectly delicious.
The shrimp pieces are authentically delicious, and the other fish pieces are worth the price.
This review is from someone who finished eating right away after all this Yen Ta Fo lover outing – I even bought a bottle of Yen Ta Fo sauce to take home!
sample_reviews_en.author: Dawin channel

sample_reviews_en.text:
Kim Nguan Fishball Noodles is a long-standing local favorite that truly deserves its Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition. The restaurant serves classic Thai-style fishball noodles with impressive consistency and quality.

The fishballs are firm yet bouncy, with a clean, fresh taste that highlights the craftsmanship of true handmade preparation. You can choose your noodles dry or with soup—the dry version comes with a flavorful mix of sauce, chili, vinegar, and peanuts, while the clear soup is light yet full of umami from the fish stock.

Don’t miss their fried fish skin—crispy, aromatic, and perfect as a side snack. Service is quick and efficient, and despite the Michelin fame, the prices remain very reasonable.
sample_reviews_en.author: Wisanu Tuntawiroon

sample_reviews_en.text:
The fish ball noodle soup tasted good; the fish balls had a chewy texture. If you like that style, you'll love it. I ordered the dry spicy noodle soup, and the noodles were soft and chewy, with a good flavor and a fragrant chili paste aroma. The bowl I ordered seemed to be a special serving, but personally, I felt the amount of fish balls wasn't very generous. The price was 75 baht.

Overall, the taste was good. The restaurant is located roadside on Rama 5 Road, inside a furniture store.

The highlight fish balls that I found particularly delicious were the shrimp balls and the fish dumplings. I really liked the taste, aroma, and texture of these.
sample_reviews_en.author: tome Nattapong Worapivut

sample_reviews_en.text: On Tuesday, August 25th, 2026 (if I'm not mistaken), I ordered Yen Ta Fo (Thai noodle soup) with thick noodles. What I received was one round fish ball, two pieces of crispy squid, and a large amount of what appeared to be boiled jellyfish that was very hard. There was only one fish ball. I'm wondering if the restaurant has reduced the amount of fish balls. I've been eating there since the restaurant first opened, and this seems strange. I admit I used to eat there every week, more than twice a week. I would like the owner to check on the staff.
sample_reviews_en.author: Siraprapa Chosawat

restaurants.name: Aroy Tatien อร่อย ท่าเตียน
restaurants.address:

99 Maha Rat Rd, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text:
Beware of the beer offer: 109฿ is essentially for one (!) draft beer, not three, so all three cost 218฿, which only makes sense if you're really craving beer. That's why I'm only giving it four stars, because the food is very good and plentiful:

The Combo Set 3 with the Boat Noodles and (in our case) coconut root salad, ice cream, and a small portion of mango sticky rice is more filling than you'd expect.

The service was excellent, by the way, but still only four stars because the beer offer is somewhat deliberately (?!) unclear.

We were the first ones in the restaurant, and it got increasingly crowded afterward, so it's quite possible the wait time could be longer.
sample_reviews_th.author: Roland M.

sample_reviews_th.text: It tasted good, but the price was a bit high. I think it was around 89฿ for this bowl, if I remember correctly. But it's acceptable considering the location. The restaurant has air conditioning, the wait wasn't long, and the taste was really good. Very delicious.
sample_reviews_th.author: uoou

sample_reviews_en.text:
#DeliciousThaTien... Air-conditioned boat noodle shop. A small shop, but the taste is surprisingly good. A real gem!

If you're strolling around Tha Tien and craving a good bowl of boat noodles, you can stop by without hesitation. While the price is around 100+ baht, similar to noodles in a shopping mall, the portions are generous. Plus, the view of Wat Arun in the beautiful sunlight in that alley makes it well worth it.

The broth is flavorful and perfectly seasoned – a balanced salty, savory, and sour taste with just the right amount of spiciness. The blood pudding is added in just the right amount, and the noodles are cooked perfectly, not too soft.

The meatballs are bouncy and high-quality. The fresh meat is tender, the stewed meat isn't incredibly soft, but it's braised to a rich, savory flavor.

In short, the shop is packed with both Thais and foreigners… Chinese and Westerners at the next table all nodded and smiled after taking their first bite. It makes us Thais happy that Thai boat noodles are truly famous worldwide!
sample_reviews_en.author: topinito S

sample_reviews_en.text: This is my favorite boat noodle restaurant❤️ I was wandering around Wat Arun because it was hot and I was tired, so I was dragged into this place, and the food was really deliciousㅠㅠ The servers were friendly, and the store was cool and cozy, but clean and had a great atmosphere. It's great even if you go alone. If you want to eat boat noodles, you should definitely go here!! The price is reasonable, and I will definitely stop by and eat here when I go back to Thailand. It's a shame, but I would have ordered more if I wasn't fullㅠㅠ It's a taste that no Korean would ever dislike. Trust me, you should definitely go!! I'm not writing this because someone else ordered it.
sample_reviews_en.author: Paris

sample_reviews_en.text: The restaurant has two floors and is always crowded. The noodle soup has an unfamiliar flavor, but it's alright after a while. The pork isn't as tender as I'd hoped; it's a bit chewy. I ordered it without meatballs, but they still included them. The lime juice, however, is delicious – good flavor, fragrant, not too sweet, and refreshingly sour.
sample_reviews_en.author: SALiN

sample_reviews_en.text: Aroy Tha Tian is a small local eatery near Tha Tian Pier, offering simple and tasty Thai dishes at reasonable prices. The food is flavorful and served quickly, making it a convenient stop after visiting nearby temples. The atmosphere is casual and local, perfect for a quick and satisfying meal in the riverside area.
sample_reviews_en.author: Tony Tran

sample_reviews_en.text:
A really simple and fuss free store.
Had simple and simply delicious boat noodle after the Thai costume photo shoot.

Air condition, clean place and reallt yummy boat noodle. Go for the dried version with medium spiciness if you have strong taste palette.

If u are a fan of Thong smith, this will be for u!
sample_reviews_en.author: Kesen. Kesen

sample_reviews_en.text: This is truly amazing! This set is my absolute favorite. The dessert is delicious, the ice cream is incredibly melt-in-your-mouth, and it pairs perfectly with the mango. The noodles are cooked perfectly, and the meat in the broth is barely seasoned. The Thai tea is also spot-on. Highly recommended!
sample_reviews_en.author: Srilak Chanthon

restaurants.name: Tamil Nadu
restaurants.address:

11 Si Lom Rd, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
Hands down the best Indian restaurant we have been to in Bangkok. The owner and staff personally took care of our group of 15 (including kids), suggested delicious foods, portions were amazing. The Idly, Dosa, Sambhar and the Biryani were to die for, but more than the food, it was the people and service that mattered more.

Also, we found out that the restaurant owner also offers tourism activities, we were able to purchase discounted tickets to the Safari World through them - smooth transaction and they sent all the tickets in minutes.

In fact, the owner was so kind that they did not even charge my wife for 2 biscuit packets that she picked up when we were about to leave.

Highly recommend going here if you are in Bangkok.
sample_reviews_en.author: Vasanthan Ramakrishnan

sample_reviews_en.text:
Great to see Tamil Nadu (TN) is still up and running and attracting a diverse range of customers.

TN is a southern Indian food stalwart in Bangkok and I like the fact that not much has changed in the 15+ years I have eaten there.

Highly recommend the dosais, dosas, voothappams, curries, samosas, and parottas. The thali is also generous and tasty. The mango lassi is also a must have beverage to counter some of the heat and spice of the dishes.

Although he wasn’t there, when I last visited, I also enjoy chatting with the patriarch of the family who own TN. He is a warm, kind, funny soul.
sample_reviews_en.author: Steve Meng Yee

sample_reviews_en.text:
We wanted Indian food so I researched where we could walk to from our hotel for a good meal!  I chose this place based on past reviews and we were so pleased!
How lovely to enjoy such tasty authentic food in a family owned restaurant.  Honestly, everything was so yummy and the service was quick and so friendly.  We even got talking with the people at the next table whom clearly also enjoyed their meal.
I also thought it was nice they let us bring our little dog in too.  We highly recommend this restaurant if you want reasonably priced authentic Indian food in a simple setting.
sample_reviews_en.author: Tania Reiher

sample_reviews_en.text:
Some of my friends recommended this place the previous day for parotta and mutton curry and I exactly ordered that though I wanted to have idly or dosai .
But I have to say it was a great experience. Parotta was so soft , crispy and not oily.  The mutton curry was delicious, though I am not a fan of big mutton pieces . Mild spicy and tasty for the parota.
The onion sambal with the chillis made a perfect combination for the dish .
Had masala tea and it was so good as I used to have in Chennai .
Overall a good brunch for me :)
Hope to have other dishes soon in the coming days .
sample_reviews_en.author: P K

sample_reviews_en.text:
This place is 1/2 in Silom 11 soi inside a small soi the restaurant is middle of the soi.

This Tamil Naidu is dive place and the food is good but can be better.

The Masala Dosa is good price so most people come here as the pricing is good.

if you are looking for affordable eats .. this would be the place.

Make sure you follow us, Follow Fauzia around Bangkok.... honest, authentic and real.
You can find Follow Fauzia on IG, FB and of course our YT channel has over 700 videos all vlogs on food reviews plus YT shorts are plenty. 💚💚🩷💚💚💚🩷🩷🩷🩷🩷💚💚💚
sample_reviews_en.author: Follow Fauzia

sample_reviews_en.text:
Tried on a local recommendation and absolutely love this place! The food is so good, fresh, home cooked, served in minutes, excellent portions and good value for money.

The vegetarian thali is my personal go to, and the roti 👌🏼 I am veggie but friend raves about both the chicken and the mutton curries. Great friendly personal service too and has a menu with photos if you ask or are unsure.

Don’t let the exterior put you off - not a fancy place and kind of up a back alleyway and may not look open from outside. Could happily eat here daily.
sample_reviews_en.author: Eleanor Vidsan

sample_reviews_en.text: Place is exceptional and I’m not an expert in Indian food but I own restaurants and this place made me very satisfied and happy. It is Halal so that’s a big plus but nonetheless, the moment you step in the restaurant, the home-cooking style kind of aroma will hit you hard no matter where you actually came from. Food has an excellent balance which will let you enjoy all the flavors all at once without any overshadowing the other. I am lucky that I love not far from here so I am definitely gonna be a regular here. 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
sample_reviews_en.author: Victor August

sample_reviews_en.text:
Serving some of the best Indian food in Bangkok! 😍 The taste, quality, and pricing are honestly amazing—you rarely find such authentic flavor at such good prices.

The dosa and rice dishes are a must-try 🥞🍚—fresh, flavorful, and full of authentic South Indian taste. The food feels comforting and homely, especially if you’re craving Indian food while traveling.

Great taste, great portions, and great value for money. Definitely a must-visit place in Bangkok for Indian food lovers! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
sample_reviews_en.author: Mehul Batra

restaurants.name: Thai Heng Li Restaurant
restaurants.address:

154 ถนนอัษฎางค์ ซอย ธีรปัตย์ 4, Wang Burapha Phirom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text: I ordered stir-fried beef with basil and a fried egg, extra rice. The rice portion was the same, the beef was soggy, and the taste was extremely salty; stir-fried beef with soy sauce would have been better. The bill came to 80฿ for that small portion of rice and a fried egg that shouldn't have cost more than 10฿, totaling 70฿ for the stir-fried beef with basil. They make you write your order on a piece of paper when ordering.
sample_reviews_th.author: Yao Yao

sample_reviews_en.text:
I'd seen this place in reviews and bookmarked it a long time ago, never thinking I'd get a chance to try it.

Today, I visited the city's main shrine and checked out some nearby locations I'd bookmarked, and that's how I found this restaurant.

The two elderly ladies running the place were incredibly friendly and welcoming. The restaurant is located on a corner next to a building, with tables and chairs set up around the house.

Almost all the dishes were delicious. Personally, I thought the basil chicken wasn't quite as good as I'd hoped, just average, but everything else was excellent. The wok-fried dishes had a wonderful aroma from being cooked over a high heat over a charcoal stove. The food came out very quickly – less than 5 minutes per dish if you're hungry! The prices were great, comparable to regular street food, but with better taste and ingredients. We ordered 6 dishes for 310 baht.

There's parking next to the restaurant. Just roll down your window and tell the ladies, and they'll remove the barrier for you to park safely (about 2 cars). You can also find parking at the street entrance, but it'll be a short walk.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pongpure

sample_reviews_en.text:
When I was staying nearby, I went for lunch because it had high ratings, and it was excellent. It's not the kind of restaurant you'd travel a long distance to for a leisurely meal, but if it were closer, I'd frequent it. I recommend adding an egg to your dish (both thin omelet and fried egg). Many locals get takeout.

When I stayed nearby again, it was the hot season, so I got takeout twice and ate leisurely in the hotel garden. The yaumusen was less watery and the best I've ever had. I plan to try the ski (I was so intrigued watching them prepare it that they told me the name) next time. The usual menu items were consistently delicious.

I stopped by to check it out and got takeout. The restaurant was even more lively than before, with more seating, and the chef's mother, whom I'd been worried about since the restaurant closed, seemed well. The opening hours also seem a little longer, indicating its popularity. You're asked to write your order on paper, but there's an English menu.
sample_reviews_en.author: 天羽庸子

sample_reviews_en.text:
Traditional charcoal-grilled made-to-order dishes with rice: pork, chicken, beef, or seafood, all priced at 60 baht except for crispy pork which is 70 baht.

The stir-fried vermicelli with soy sauce and beef was good, fragrant from the wok, and the beef wasn't tough, although some pieces still had some tendons. The vegetables were tender (4.5).
The stir-fried basil beef had good pieces of beef, not tough, and used chopped chilies instead of pounded ones. It was mildly spicy (4.3).
The seafood with garlic was also decent (4.1).

Free crispy pork rinds are available upon request (they're not given unless you ask). They give a generous portion. It wasn't crowded in the morning.
sample_reviews_en.author: Almagiro 1

sample_reviews_en.text:
I've walked past this restaurant before and seen many foreign customers eating there. I was surprised, but never decided to try it. Today, I finally got to.

The owner is an elderly lady who cooks every dish herself. She seems to have a lot of experience. I ordered minced pork basil stir-fry with rice and added a fried egg. The wait wasn't long, even though the restaurant was busy. When it arrived, it looked delicious. They were generous with the basil leaves and ingredients. This restaurant uses chopped bird's eye chilies, not pounded chilies, so the flavor was mild, not too spicy, and very easy to eat. The fried egg was perfectly crispy, which I loved.
sample_reviews_en.author: วิน วิน พลัส

sample_reviews_en.text:
This restaurant uses a charcoal stove for stir-frying. They have crispy pork, but I think the shrimp and squid are delicious – fresh, large, and generous portions. The whole meal cost 390 baht.
Dishes start at 60 baht each. People were coming and going constantly (we came on a holiday). 🚗 Parking is a bit of a gamble, or you can park near the Land Department. The owner is kind and gives generous portions. There are several tables in front of the shop, probably 7 to 10 tables. The food didn't take long to arrive. People kept stopping by to buy food.
sample_reviews_en.author: Im migrant

sample_reviews_en.text:
This made-to-order food stall offers a variety of dishes. There's only one cook, so you might have to wait a bit. The stall is located in an alley, with tables set up on the sidewalk...
The food is a little bland, but it has that authentic, childhood-style made-to-order taste. Stir-fried over a high charcoal fire, which I really love. Generous portions at reasonable prices. It gets busy before noon, so you might have to wait a while... I'm full.
Updated 9/5/69: Haven't eaten here in a long time. This was a full feast!
sample_reviews_en.author: ChubbyArin

sample_reviews_en.text: Really looked forward to trying this one, got here at 4pm on a Sunday and it's closed, which I think is very sad, I drove 30 minutes to try her noodles. On Google maps it says it's open until 6pm but that wasn't the case today. It gets 4 stars because I'm still convinced that the noodles are good. But sad that it was closed even though it should have been open.
sample_reviews_en.author: cristian

restaurants.name: Baan Ice บ้านไอซ์ เซ็นทรัลลาดพร้าว
restaurants.address:

ศูนย์การค้า เซ็นทรัลลาดพร้าว ชั้น 4, 1691 Phahonyothin Rd, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
My first time dining at Baan Ice was an incredibly impressive experience, from the taste of the food to the restaurant's concept.

Every dish showcased the high quality of the ingredients. The flavors were authentically spicy Southern Thai, yet well-balanced and easy to eat.
I particularly enjoyed the selection of rare, traditional dishes, offering a truly immersive local culinary experience. It wasn't just familiar Southern Thai food; these dishes had their own stories and unique characteristics.

Another highlight was the restaurant's storytelling approach, emphasizing the sourcing of its ingredients. The presentation highlighted the use of natural and organic ingredients, making the meal not only delicious but also instilling a sense of peace and confidence in the quality of the source.

The price was reasonable, considering the quality of the ingredients, the meticulous preparation, and the overall concept. This restaurant is perfect for those who appreciate high-quality, authentic Thai cuisine, want dishes with a rich history and story, and are mindful of the environment. I will definitely return if I have the chance.
sample_reviews_en.author: SK Katair

sample_reviews_en.text:
The food was surprisingly salty. For example, the stir-fried cabbage with fish sauce was unexpectedly salty.
The shrimp paste chili dip is much better at street markets; it has a much stronger shrimp paste flavor (the one at Top Supermarket is much better). This one was too salty, and while it seemed to have some kind of texture, it lacked the shrimp paste flavor.
The stir-fried crab meat with yellow chilies was served in a very small portion; I had to ask if this was considered a large size, and it lacked the fragrant yellow chili aroma it should have.

The stir-fried Gnetum leaves and the pork chunks were okay.

It seems the taste has deteriorated because this is a branch restaurant located in a mall.

However, the staff were very well-trained and provided excellent service.
sample_reviews_en.author: Weerapon Nitigultanont

sample_reviews_en.text:
Southern Thai food with excellent flavors and premium ingredients.
_Grandma's Khanom Jeen (rice noodles) with Southern-style coconut milk curry and chili paste (both spicy and sweet versions available), served with vegetables, was truly delicious.
_Winged bean salad, with a perfect balance of sour, spicy, and sweet flavors, served with large, fresh shrimp and boiled eggs.
_Fried squid, crispy and delicious, very addictive.
_Fish cakes, made with real fish, not overly chewy, with a slightly sweet taste.
_Fried sun-dried barracuda, a large fish with plenty of meat, not too salty. This was my least favorite dish.
The food is pricey, but definitely worth it.
The staff provided excellent service and helpful recommendations.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nana Relax

sample_reviews_en.text: This Southern Thai restaurant serves delicious food, every dish is excellent. Most of the staff are foreigners, but the service is great and the food comes out very quickly. That day I ordered stir-fried pork ribs with chili paste, crab egg chili paste, and salted fried chicken. Everything was delicious, although the salted fried chicken was a little dry. It would have been nice to have chili sauce as well, but there wasn't. We didn't ask for it anyway because it was delicious with the crab egg chili paste. On that day, the restaurant also gave out bags of mangosteen that you could choose yourself. The mangosteen was beautiful and incredibly delicious! I was very impressed.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nicky2v Tan

sample_reviews_en.text: This is actually a restaurant I used to frequent. If I was craving spicy Thai food, I'd always think of it first. But since I'm starting to be able to handle less spicy food, I haven't been here as often. My go-to dishes are fried shrimp heads and stir-fried pork cartilage with red curry paste. Other than that, I rotate them around. This time, my recommended dish is fried catfish. I ordered the catfish with red curry paste, which was delicious. However, it seems like I haven't eaten it in a long time, so the price and portions have changed quite a bit. From being reasonably expensive, it suddenly becomes much more expensive. 🤭🙏
sample_reviews_en.author: Tanate Ruangviwattanaphan

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant was pretty full, mostly Thai families and couples enjoying a Saturday lunch.

It was a good menu, only Thai dishes, and a bit different than many Thai places that seem to serve everything.
They had salads, soups, curries, several fish dishes.
The dining room was very nicely furnished, clean with both booths and table seating.
The staff were very attentive and friendly.

The food was very good, nice size portions and reasonably priced considering it’s in Central a very nice restaurant.

I read that it can be very busy at peak dinner times, but there though crowded there was no wait for lunch.

I will go back.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pairinmas Buasomboon

sample_reviews_en.text:
Tried this restaurant for the first time. Was pleasantly surprised by the quality and taste of the food. Was pretty southern Thai type of food.
A group of 6 pax, we ordered:
1. Fried baeliang vegetable with egg - very good
2. BFC (Bangkok fried chicken) - very crispy and fragrant we all loved it
3. Thai fish cakes - loads of fish meat used, very good
4. Sambal petai with pork - lovely
5. Green curry chicken - spicy and nice the way I love it
6. Fried omelet with crab meat - delicious

We wanted to order the tom yum soup however they ran out of mushrooms so we didn’t try.

Overall, was good food and worth going back.
sample_reviews_en.author: Paul Ryan Soh

sample_reviews_en.text:
The food was amazing, especially if you love Southern Thai flavors. I really enjoyed the Sator Kapi Goong—the shrimp paste with stink beans was packed with flavor. The Khai Palo was rich and comforting. The Gaeng Som Pla Krapong was spicy, tangy, and full of depth—definitely one of the highlights. Even the shrimp head was delicious, and the Thai-style omelette was simple but done really well.

Highly recommended if you’re craving authentic Southern Thai food in a nice mall setting. Great for both family meals and casual hangouts.
sample_reviews_en.author: Chen E.

restaurants.name: Yum Rod Sab
restaurants.address:

57 Charoen Nakhon 9 Alley, Khlong Ton Sai, Khlong San, Bangkok 10600, Thailand

sample_reviews_th.text: This place is amazing!!!! Get the fried chicken with herbs (ไก่ทอดสมุนไพร). It will change your life!!! No kidding.
sample_reviews_th.author: Kristen Chuenchum

sample_reviews_en.text:
It was surprisingly tasty! We found this place randomly because the original place that we planned was closed, so we did quick research for resto nearby and this was it. Not a single moment I regret it.

The place was inside the alley, very hidden, because you have to go by foot to go inside the restaurant. Not that far from the road tho, if you come with taxi 👌🏻

When we walked through, we saw another couple just got off the taxi and it turned out they went to the same place as we did 😂.

First time we entered the resto, it was empty, because we had a late lunch ~2PM. But, i didn't hesitate to eat here because once we arrived there were bunch of people just finished and their plates were very clean, then i just knew it was good.

We ordered the pork meat, tom yam and papaya salad for people of two. The meat perfectly cooked, the tom yam taste rich but not to sour (which the way i like) and lastly their papaya salad was so refreshing! with a bit crunchyness with the nuts. All in all, BEST lunch ever in Bangkok 🔥🔥

Worth to try if you are nearby and looking for complete Thai lunch 👌🏻👌🏻👌🏻
sample_reviews_en.author: Michelle Nathania

sample_reviews_en.text:
🌟This is my first time leaving a Google review.
I've been here two days in a row and will be back again tomorrow.
This is my favorite restaurant I've been to in Bangkok.
If you like meat, the fried pork belly is amazing. The corn somtam and grilled pork neck are so delicious, I highly recommend them!!!

I fell in love with the fried pork belly and corn somtam on my first visit.
The next day, I had the grilled pork neck and corn somtam.
It was just as delicious, chewy, and savory as ever!!
