restaurants.name: Kway Chap J' Noy
restaurants.address:

116/2 Soi King Chan, Wat Phraya Krai, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok 10120, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text: The kway chap was amazing! It was my first time there, and I didn't listen to the menu beforehand when I ordered (later I found out you can choose between chewy and soft noodles). I loved the chewy noodles, they were perfect. And the crispy pork... oh my god, if you love crispy pork, order the kway chap with only crispy pork – there's so much! Just thinking about it makes my mouth water. It's truly beyond words. My third bowl came with perfectly cooked offal – liver, intestines, lungs, cartilage – nothing smelly. It's hard to find a place that cooks this well and makes it so tender. A slight drawback: the owner chatted a lot (with her friends), so the food was a bit slow to come out. It was delicious eating at the restaurant and equally delicious eating at home. I went on a holiday; I don't know where to park on a weekday. Finally, I'm not sure if this is a thick or clear broth kway chap, it's kind of in between. I want to eat it again! So good!
sample_reviews_en.author: aunne’ gyeomie

sample_reviews_en.text: This is a small noodle soup (kuy chap) shop located in a row of buildings at the beginning of Chan Road. It's an old, established shop. If you plan to visit, it's best to come before noon because the food tends to sell out quickly. As for the taste, from what I tried, it was excellent. The ingredients were cut into pieces that were neither too big nor too small, just the right size. The crispy pork was also very good – definitely a highlight. Overall, the broth was flavorful, not overly salty or sweet. The noodles were firm and chewy, making them enjoyable to eat. The offal had no unpleasant smell. On the day I visited, I had to wait quite a while after ordering because there were many takeout orders. Considering the portion size, the price is reasonable and worth the visit. Parking is a bit difficult as the street isn't very wide, but you might be able to squeeze in along the side of the road.
sample_reviews_en.author: panya tharathipphitak

sample_reviews_en.text:
Je Noi's Kuay Jab (Soi Chan 51) is another highly-rated restaurant I found through a search app. I chose the Charoen Krung Road area and nearby. Arriving at 2 PM, the place was still busy with many customers and delivery drivers. Despite the crowd, the food service was quite slow.

〰️Kuay Jab with everything: The noodles were soft, and the broth was mild and flavorful. Those who prefer milder flavors will enjoy it. The offal was good, large pieces, and not gamey, except for the pork intestines which still had a slight odor. ⭐⭐⭐
〰️Small plate of crispy pork: Crispy, slightly salty, delicious with sweet soy sauce. The pork was chopped up with a mix of fat and meat. ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Overall, I give it 3.5 stars. It's better than most restaurants, but not outstanding. The food service was a bit slow, and since I couldn't round up the rating, I gave it that score.
sample_reviews_en.author: MrStew LuiRoj

sample_reviews_en.text: This is a shop I stumbled upon by chance. This kway chap (rice noodle soup) shop is a hidden gem in the Chan Road area. Everything feels incredibly fresh and delicious: the noodles are soft and fragrant, the intestines are tender and flavorful, the liver and heart are soft and aromatic, and the crispy pork is perfectly crunchy. Especially the broth, which is perfectly balanced and savory – a truly blissful taste. I challenge you to try it and see if you can resist slurping up the broth! I, for one, couldn't resist the delicious aroma and ordered another bowl because I still wasn't satisfied. Every bowl and every serving is meticulously made by the owner, who patiently assists when needed. If you're interested in trying it, be prepared to pay cash; there's no parking. It's a pleasant walk there and back.
sample_reviews_en.author: Somchai Anantnakin

sample_reviews_en.text: The best in the area, paying attention to detail. I told them no MSG, and the staff clearly and emphatically told their boss. The broth is made from real pork bones; I saw with my own eyes they used a whole pot of pork rib bones. All the offal is thoroughly cleaned. Truly delicious. The crispy pork is excellent. P.S. It's crowded, so there's a long wait. Some people call in orders for pickup, and they make those too. Some people misunderstand and think they're cutting in line, which is bad. And those who want to deduct stars for parking spaces are another problem. It's not a fancy restaurant, it's a small shop, and it's very popular, so of course there's a wait. Use your brains!
sample_reviews_en.author: Pichai Thitiwong

sample_reviews_en.text:
Jae Noi's Kuay Jab (Thick Broth)
A famous shop on Chan Road, near Bridge 5.
The shop has moved slightly from its original building.
Opens at 11:30 AM.
They won't sell until then.
The staff can be a bit abrupt in their speech.
The kuay jab has a moderate flavor.
Not as rich as thick broth kuay jab.
The spice aroma isn't very strong.
But it doesn't have a strong peppery smell like the clear broth version.
It's just average, but edible.
The owner keeps it very clean.
The offal has no smell at all.
The crispy pork has less fat than other places.
The noodles are perfectly cooked, not too hard and not too soft.
sample_reviews_en.author: Piya Jirapapongpan

sample_reviews_en.text:
The portions are getting smaller and smaller. There's no stomach or kidney anymore, just one piece of intestine, one piece of tongue, one piece of liver, two pieces of egg (half an egg), and two pieces of tofu for 50 baht. Crispy pork is 75 baht per portion. The only thing that remains the same is the noodles.😅😅 It's a shame, I've been a long-time customer.
Compared to Mr. Joe's, the price difference is only 10 baht, but you get all the ingredients you ordered, the offal pieces are bigger, and the taste is better.👍
sample_reviews_en.author: saifha bunya

sample_reviews_en.text: The noodle soup and crispy pork were quite delicious, deserving 5 stars. However, I'm deducting 1 star because the queuing system was terrible. They relied on memory, making mistakes and even prioritizing people who ordered before me. It was chaotic, and I waited almost an hour for my food. I recommend avoiding lunchtime; come before or after. There's some parking available along the fence across the street. Overall, I still recommend it.
sample_reviews_en.author: akkharanij Jiamniyom

restaurants.name: ศูนย์รวมอาหารอิสลามแยกทางรถไฟ พัทยา
restaurants.address:

WWP4+3H3 ซอยสยามคันทรีคลับ แยกทางรถไฟ Bang Lamung District, Chon Buri 20150, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text: There are several Halal Muslim restaurants near the train station in Pattaya. When I visited, there were four open: a biryani rice shop, a made-to-order food shop, a roti and dumpling shop, a boxed meal shop, a Middle Eastern salad shop, and a kebab shop. The food tasted good, the prices were reasonable, and the service was good. The chicken dumplings were delicious. They also have Middle Eastern salad, which I bought to take home. It was busy at lunchtime, so I had to wait a while. Overall, it was good. Anyone passing by should give it a try.
sample_reviews_en.author: BKP2563

sample_reviews_en.text: Almost 3 years stay in Pattaya (2012-2015). One of the best stall for breakfast & lunch. Beef soup, Kao man & some many choices. Aroi mak. We also can get halal food at restaurant near to mosque at Noen Plubwan Road (Dar Al Abror, Nurool Yakeen). Another restaurant to enjoy halal Thai food is at Muslim seafood. I will revisit there while visit Pattaya soon.
sample_reviews_en.author: Amri Isfar

sample_reviews_en.text: This restaurant serves delicious rice dishes. They have a variety of food, including biryani rice. Their roti is very tasty, and the grilled meat skewers are delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: Kornkamon Nuchsiri

sample_reviews_en.text: The food was delicious, especially the duck stir-fry and mataba. It's a small food court by the railway tracks. I'll definitely stop by again if I'm in the area.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pongsak Matragool

sample_reviews_en.text: Walked from Pattaya Train station to here for lunch, next to a school. There are few halal stalls here serving different kind of food options.
sample_reviews_en.author: fr

sample_reviews_en.text:
A wide variety of food.
Eat at a rice and curry shop; the food is delicious and the prices are reasonable.
sample_reviews_en.author: Sareeya Soomad

sample_reviews_en.text: The food was delicious and the prices were great, the only downside was the hot weather.
sample_reviews_en.author: Wow wow Mochi

sample_reviews_en.text: There are many good Muslim food options, both in Soi Mabyailia and Soi Pornprapanimit.
sample_reviews_en.author: LOZAN SB

restaurants.name: Sandy's
restaurants.address:

Sathorn Conner, UG Floor, 46 Soi Phiphat, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
One of the decent fried chicken restaurants that is located in Sathorn soi 8.

The fried chicken comes as 3 choices; wing, tender, boneless with few different flavours. Love the crispy texture of fried chicken yet still contains enough moist of chicken meat. The dipping sauce is interesting part which is nicely prepared and available in few options.

Smoke duck salad is so refreshing. Calamari goes well with dill ranch dressing. The side dishes serving along are relatively small but taste good especially curly fries.

However, my favourite dish is Panang spaghetti with prawns which uses Thai red curry. The creamy Panang sause is perfectly cooked as full of spice and aroma then mixing with soft fresh spaghetti and generous size of prawns. This twisted Thai version of pasta is a Must Try!

Recommend to book in advance as tables and seats are quite limited. Payment methods are cash or bank tranfer, no credit card option.
sample_reviews_en.author: Apichart Dausiri

sample_reviews_en.text:
I absolutely love this cozy spot—Sandy’s! They specialize in fried chicken and craft beer, and one thing I adore is how you can choose your chicken part—wings, tenders, or boneless.

The 𝑪𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒎𝒆𝒍 𝒇𝒍𝒂𝒗𝒐𝒖𝒓𝒆𝒅 𝒄𝒉𝒊𝒄𝒌𝒆𝒏 ? Insane. It had the perfect balance of sweet and salty, packed with rich flavor. The 𝑵𝒂𝒔𝒉𝒗𝒊𝒍𝒍𝒆 𝑪𝒉𝒊𝒄𝒌𝒆𝒏 was a flawless spicy blend of seasoning infused with hot oil. I’ve heard great things about the Lemon Pepper flavor, but I haven’t tried it yet. Pairing the chicken with the 𝑯𝒐𝒏𝒆𝒚 𝑴𝒖𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒅 𝑫𝒊𝒑 was so so good, though the mustard was a bit overpowering—so go for the 𝒓𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒉 if you prefer something milder!

And don’t even get me started on the 𝑷𝒂𝒏𝒂𝒏𝒈 𝑺𝒉𝒓𝒊𝒎𝒑 𝑷𝒂𝒔𝒕𝒂... Words don’t do it justice! It was creamy with a subtle curry flavor, topped with juicy prawns, and somehow, it wasn’t ‘jelak’.

A must visit!! Check out @foodiefeyf for food review <3
sample_reviews_en.author: faith

sample_reviews_en.text:
Homey-style fried chicken, cute and cozy decor, great vibe, perfect for chatting with friends. Enjoy the fried chicken, savory dips, and a cold drink – it's the ultimate combination!

Five dipping sauces available:
Ranch (mild and savory), Mentaiko (fragrant with fish roe), Honey Mustard, Spicy Mayo, and Smoked Mayo (rich and smoky).

🍞Ikura on Toast: Grilled toast topped with a generous amount of salmon roe – pure bliss!
🍝Vongole: Clam pasta with a well-balanced flavor.
🥗Smoked Duck Salad: Smoked duck breast salad with a refreshing dressing to cut through the richness.
Finally, a refreshing Yuzu & Ume high ball.

Note: Tables are a bit close together, so reservations are recommended.
🚗Parking is limited. If coming by BTS, get off at Chong Nonsi station.
sample_reviews_en.author: กินเล่นๆป้ะ

sample_reviews_en.text:
Crispy, hot fried chicken available in wings, tender, and boneless options. I ordered wings and tender.
*Regular tender: Normal, plain taste.
*Boneless lemon pepper: Strong lemon aroma, fragrant and tasty, but not amazing.
*Various dips enhance the flavor of the chicken.
*Smoked duck salad: Delicious, good dressing.
*Calamari: Crispy and delicious.
*Gambas al Ajillo (Shrimps with garlic, dried chili, olive oil, and butter): Plain taste, unfortunately not fresh shrimp, seemed like frozen.
*Truffle Fettuccine Alfredo: Creamy, well-balanced, delicious, perfectly cooked.
*Good service, standard, attentive to customers.
*The restaurant isn't large, but comfortable seating.
sample_reviews_en.author: Lara Linh

sample_reviews_en.text:
The Nashville-flavored fried chicken is delicious, and the lemon sauce helps cut through the richness. The Ranch-flavored fried chicken is also fantastic and goes well with the chicken. All the side dishes are tasty, but if I had to choose, I'd pick the curly fries.

Besides the fried chicken, the duck salad is also incredibly delicious. The other dishes are good too, but none are as amazing as the fried chicken.

The caramel-flavored fried chicken is a bit too sweet for my liking. I ordered it with honey mustard, which made it even sweeter. If you like sweeter flavors, you'll probably enjoy both the chicken and the sauce.
sample_reviews_en.author: bbugsbunny

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is located on a mezzanine floor and has a simple, relaxed decor. The atmosphere is great, and I especially liked that the restaurant seems to have a good ventilation system because there was no lingering oil smell after I finished eating.
I wasn't quite sure about the menu though; I'd like the restaurant to adjust the packaging so that you can order by the piece. The fried chicken tasted good; it was crispy and not dry, but personally, it wasn't amazing. The service was good. Parking is available in the plaza, but it can be difficult during rush hour because it gets crowded.
sample_reviews_en.author: N. W.

sample_reviews_en.text:
This small but cute fried chicken shop in Soi Sathorn 8 is incredibly delicious. Be sure to get there early, as there were still tables available at 11:45 AM. By noon, the place was packed and very popular.

Their main dish is fried chicken. They have a wide selection of lattes and dips. I couldn't decide, but someone recommended something for me. They were so lovely. I ordered the exact dish I ordered and was absolutely delighted. I absolutely loved their green curry dish. It was delicious, fragrant, and incredibly spicy. 💕 I'll definitely be back!
sample_reviews_en.author: Moddang

sample_reviews_en.text:
This restaurant is located at Sathorn Corner, on the second floor, to the right as you enter. The chicken is crispy and flavorful. I ordered the set menu for one, and the portion was quite large.

After choosing the chicken parts, you can select from a variety of flavors, dips, and side dishes. There are plenty of options available. I will definitely come back to try different combinations and the pasta dishes.
sample_reviews_en.author: Mint's

restaurants.name: Bún Bò Ơi - Sukhumvit 49
restaurants.address:

10 Soi Phrom Phak, Khlong Tan Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok 10110, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
This restaurant is housed in a renovated private home, and while it's typical of Thonglor, it's not cheap, but it's delicious and, above all, stylish. And, most importantly, whether it looks good on Instagram is a major factor.

You order using your smartphone while looking at the menu. While there are many restaurants where everything is done on a smartphone, it's still important to look at the paper version and feel truly at ease.

After ordering, we waited 30 minutes. The restaurant wasn't particularly busy, but perhaps there was a war going on in the kitchen, as the food took a long time to arrive.

The interior is elaborately designed, but since you can't see inside, it's difficult to call a waiter, which is frustrating.

As for the food... I often go to Vietnam on business trips, and it somehow feels different. Here, too, style takes priority, and it seems like appearance is valued over substance.

Lunch for two was 1,000 THB, as you'd expect from Thonglor.

It may be perfect for young people, but you'll need some financial means.
sample_reviews_en.author: K M

sample_reviews_en.text:
29Aug26
It was completely empty when I went there. Staff were extremely kind and friendly. They had small & Medium size noodle soups. We ordered med size noddles but it looked like small portion. Foods were OK. except the portion but I think the owner was too greedy to charge 100 baht for Singha Soda water. I have never seen any small local restaurants charge 100 baht for small Singha Soda water. You can buy 20 bottles for 190 baht at the supermarket. It was too much ! they normally charge 20-50 baht maximum at the normal or shopping mall restaurants. I was shocked to see it. Overall I think it was too expensive meal for what we had and I am sorry I cannot recommend this restaurant.  It was a foreigner tourist trap kind of restaurant. I now understand why it was completely empty.
sample_reviews_en.author: Marc Marc

sample_reviews_en.text:
They served expired food. Maybe because the restaurant is always quiet and they keep old food. The soggy spring roll has definitely gone bad. It was smelly and super sour. At first they admitted it was expired spring roll, then later they said there's pickles inside (bringing pickles out). I tasted the pickles, it wasn't even sour.

Very slow service. Staff can't speak English or Thai.

Ordered Pho 390 baht. 5 small pieces of Fried Tofu 160 baht and Bun Xao Chay 360 baht.  (These prices are before tax and service)
All tasted really bad.

By far, the worst Vietnamese food I've ever had.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pigmy Pom

sample_reviews_en.text:
Very beautiful place… quiet and authentic vibration…
Food is very delicious…
The staff are super kind and polite. Although they were treated badly by an impolite, arrogant customer sitting behind me, they patiently absorbed his unethical behaviour.
I believe the phrase “the customer is always right” should be: “The customer will not be right if he does not behave right.” For we are all brothers and sisters.

Yes yes it is recommended🤩
Love to Vietnam and it's nice people. 💜
sample_reviews_en.author: StarshaSunYa

sample_reviews_en.text:
First of all, food is a 5/10. Veggies were acceptable, but the meats were dry and chewy. Portion given was skimpy, not enough even after I ordered extra pork. For 1 special bun bo hue and 2 drinks, my bill was 830 baht.
If you're hungry and just wants vietnamese food there are a lot more affordable places. The price is too high for the quality and taste of food. Even the drinks are expensive. 1st and last time. Nothing memorable to report.
sample_reviews_en.author: Jenna Carroll

sample_reviews_en.text:
French bread with pork – I personally don't like it.
The price is high, and the quality isn't comparable to other Vietnamese dishes.
Unfortunately, we all found the food mediocre and decided not to visit again.

I don't know why the restaurant has such high ratings. The menu selection is limited, and the prices are about 80-100 baht more expensive than typical Vietnamese restaurants. The ambiance is simple and unremarkable.
sample_reviews_en.author: DODO GG

sample_reviews_en.text:
Very delicious Vietnamese food.
I've personally traveled to Vietnam over 10 times, and the food at this restaurant is truly delicious. Above all, the staff are very friendly.
There are no sidewalks, so it can be a bit of a struggle to get there, but you can drink Saigon beer and it seems like it would be nice to relax and enjoy a drink on the terrace.
sample_reviews_en.author: kejime kakeuma

sample_reviews_en.text: As a regular customer I’m so disappointed at the latest price adjustment. I used to go there every week to have Bun Bo Hue at 200 THB and now they have updated the price to 390 THB which is double the price. The food has always been amazing but with this crazy price increasing, I don’t think I’m coming back. So sad.

sample_reviews_en.text: The staff member looked really grumpy today. She must be tired. The barbecue seasoning powder was way too salty, inedible, and made my kidneys tingle. The corn seasoning powder was okay.

sample_reviews_en.text: The fries and chicken here are amazing love the combination. All the add on powder is yummy too especially chilli cheese and bbq. The staffs are fast and attentive. Super yummy!

sample_reviews_en.text: The french fries were delicious, the wait wasn't long, the restaurant looked clean, and the staff provided good service.

sample_reviews_en.text: The staff were lovely, the atmosphere was beautiful, and the food arrived quickly; we didn't have to wait long.

sample_reviews_en.text: Straight fries are pretty ordinary; McDonald's shake-to-fry fries are still far superior.

sample_reviews_en.text: I ordered through Foodpanda and they gave me less ingredients than other branches. I wondered if they were saving them for themselves or being stingy. I didn't find a single fresh chili pepper at all. They only gave me half a cup of mayonnaise, and the cheesy chicken had only a tiny bit of seasoning powder – not as amazing as other branches, like the Ladprao 101 branch. I've encountered this several times and had to complain. They're really stingy with the ingredients at this branch.
sample_reviews_en.author: Kiken Yoshi Chuui suruto

sample_reviews_en.text: The food item was out of stock, but they didn't close the order. They called later to inform me that it was sold out. If I wanted to substitute another item, there would be an additional charge. When I asked to cancel the order, they refused to do it themselves, making the customer cancel it instead. Isn't that a waste of time? I've already paid, and now I have to wait for a refund. Their work is completely disorganized.
sample_reviews_en.author: LLatte Mook

sample_reviews_en.text:
I went there because it recently opened near my office.
I ordered delivery for weekday lunch.

They had a wide variety of chicken and fried foods and the portions were very generous.

It seemed to be a chain restaurant with branches in other parts of Bangkok.

The flavors were robust.

They have a wide variety of dishes, so it might be fun to order a variety of dishes and share them with others.
sample_reviews_en.author: Kori Planning

sample_reviews_en.text: The restaurant offers authentic Korean-style fried chicken with a crispy, double-fried coating that stays crunchy while keeping the meat juicy. Popular flavors such as Soy Garlic and Yangnyeom (Sweet & Spicy) are well-balanced and flavorful. Korean fried chicken is known for its light, crispy texture and signature sauces, making it different from typical fast-food fried chicken.
sample_reviews_en.author: Selena Smith

sample_reviews_en.text: The staff are very rude and have a poor attitude toward their work, especially the Thai woman who works the evening shift. She is extremely rude and shows no respect to customers. Although the food is good, the restaurant needs to change its staff.
sample_reviews_en.author: Khun Hein Saw Pyae Tun

sample_reviews_en.text: The seasoned fried chicken was a bit too sweet, but I think it's pretty close to the taste of Korean fried chicken! One downside is that they don't accept cash! I barely managed to pay in cash this time! Phew!

sample_reviews_en.text: I ordered through Grab, and the cheese dip sauce spilled all over the place. I called the restaurant to report it, but the employee hung up after answering. It's the worst service I've ever experienced.

sample_reviews_en.text: They told me to wait for 5 minutes. Half an hour passed and I still hadn't received anything. I asked again and they said 5 minutes again. This is awful, I'm very disappointed.

restaurants.address:

1695 Phahonyothin Rd, Khwaeng Chatuchak, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
I recently decided to try the dimsum buffet at this restaurant and my experience was just okay. One thing that stood out to me was the abundance of private dining spaces, catering to groups of all sizes. It's a nice option for those looking for a more intimate gathering.

The buffet menu covered a wide range of popular dimsum options, both steamed and fried. With the promise of all-you-can-eat dimsum, I expected the quantity of food to be satisfying. Unfortunately, the taste of the dishes was just average in my opinion. There were a few items that I did not enjoy, such as the large noodle with pork, honeydew lemon, and the sesame dumplings.The service was a bit confusing, even though there were only three tables occupied during my visit. It felt like there was a lack of organization or attentiveness from the staff, which affected my overall dining experience.

Considering the price of the buffet and the quality of the food and service, I don't think it's worth the value. While it's great to have a variety of dimsum options, taste and service play significant roles in fully enjoying a dining experience. Unfortunately, this restaurant fell short in those aspects.
sample_reviews_en.author: HL

sample_reviews_en.text:
📍 Located in Centara Grand at Central Plaza Ladprao Bangkok, next to Central Plaza Ladprao. Easy access via MRT or car. You can walk from the mall’s 2nd floor through the parking area directly to the restaurant.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)

Came here with my family for the all-you-can-eat dim sum buffet—very impressed. The atmosphere is nice and relaxing with Chinese background music.

🥟 Food: Excellent quality, everything tasted great
👩‍🍳 Service: Outstanding—Khun Pu was very attentive and gave great menu recommendations
🏢 Space: Large dining area, no waiting time, seated quickly

They offer both à la carte and buffet options. Dim sum prices range from 75–180 THB per dish, and the quality is definitely worth it.

Highly recommended for family dining 👍
sample_reviews_en.author: Boat Pheerawat

sample_reviews_en.text:
I had the opportunity to enjoy a Chinese dim sum buffet at *Dynasty Restaurant*, Centara Grand at Central Plaza Ladprao. The service was truly exceptional — the staff were attentive and genuinely thoughtful, which made our experience even more memorable.
When I made the reservation through Hungry Hub, I mentioned that we were dining as a team and also celebrating a birthday. I didn’t expect the staff to surprise us with a cute birthday cake — such a lovely and heartwarming gesture!
Special thanks to **P’ Ae, P’ Ploy, and P’ Nan** for their outstanding service and warm hospitality. You really made our day!
Thank you for creating such a wonderful dining experience. We truly appreciated it!
sample_reviews_en.author: Nittakan Sakulphram

sample_reviews_en.text:
This premium dim sum buffet is incredibly delicious, both in taste and atmosphere.
The wrappers are thin, the fillings are generous, and each basket is served piping hot, the aroma wafting from the moment the lid is opened.
The menu is diverse, making it enjoyable to eat without getting bored, especially the shrimp dumplings and steamed dumplings.
The price is 1,190++ baht for an all-you-can-eat buffet with no time limit. It's very worthwhile and impressive.
Besides the dim sum buffet, I highly recommend ordering the Peking duck – it's a must-try!
The skin is incredibly crispy and perfectly delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: Psstory Chanel

sample_reviews_en.text:
We had a great time with the weekend all-you-can-eat dim sum buffet at the Dynasty restaurant. My father enjoys all the dishes despite being a pretty picky eater. Staff were super attentive and responded to the food allergy notice in a very caring manner. Khun Napassorn had specially provided us with the ingredients in each dish served whether it contains prawn/shrimp which may cause allergic reaction to one of our family member.

Special gratitude to the staff; Khun A, Khun Ploy, Khun Pu, and Khun Nan. They truly made our special day memorable.

10/10 definitely coming back, worth every Baht spent.
sample_reviews_en.author: Natta Netivara

sample_reviews_en.text: The ingredients were fresh and the food tasted good. The dim sum pieces were large and just the right size. Food was served quickly. The lunch promotion is priced at 999++ which is acceptable for hotel standards. The service from the staff was average, some good, some not so good, a mix of both. I would like to see staff trained to have a consistent level of service or a uniform standard. If a customer asks what's delicious, they should be able to recommend it, not say they've never tried it. The hotel should improve the staff's knowledge and ability to recommend and remember dishes.
sample_reviews_en.author: A PARK

sample_reviews_en.text: I was very impressed. The food was delicious and high-quality. The dim sum had plenty of shrimp, and the Peking duck was flavorful. What impressed me most was the exceptional service from the staff. They were very attentive to customers. I came to celebrate my birthday without informing the restaurant beforehand. The staff saw me bringing a small bouquet of flowers to congratulate my friend on her birthday, and during the dessert course, they surprised me with a dessert with candles and sang "Happy Birthday." Thank you so much, P' Guitar, P' A, Khun P, and Nong Prik Thai 😊
sample_reviews_en.author: Sunny W

sample_reviews_en.text:
Dim Sum Buffet 999 THB/person (price includes drinks)
Choose 2 appetizers/person
Choose 1 soup/person
Unlimited dim sum, choose 1 dessert/person
The atmosphere is quite private, with private rooms available if you prefer a lot of privacy. The food is delicious, both steamed and fried. My personal favorite is the shrimp spring rolls with mango sauce; it's unique and interesting.
The service is attentive. Even though it's a private setting, the staff are always ready to serve. On my visit, I met Pook and A, who provided excellent and friendly service, always smiling.
sample_reviews_en.author: Smithti Teeratrakul

restaurants.address:

1330 Banthat Thong Rd, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
I didn't intend to eat at this restaurant, but I vaguely remembered seeing reviews, so I decided to try it. I was shocked by the service from the foreign waiters, but I tried not to think too much about it. Then I was shocked by the orange stains on our dishes, and our whole group was stained too. We bravely wiped them off with tissues.

But what shocked me the most was that there weren't a single pair of tongs on the conveyor belt. Customers were supposed to use their own tongs to pick food from the conveyor belt. The condition of the food on the belt – the color of the meat, the smell of seafood, and the vegetables floating in the water – was appalling. I even saw people using chopsticks to pick up raw food (marinated chicken) from the conveyor belt.

I think the restaurant should at least have some basic understanding of public health and the contamination of raw food.

Finally, I just want the restaurant to reflect on its own shortcomings and start improving from small, simple things.

I don't blame the restaurant at all. I told my friends that we must have been unlucky today to come to this restaurant. Thank you.
sample_reviews_en.author: Sukeroku&Jiro

sample_reviews_en.text: I was unimpressed from the moment I arrived. I informed them that there were two of us. Initially, they told us to sit down. I said I needed to retrieve my helmet first. Less than a minute later, they came back and told us to use the QueueQueue app to reserve a table, even though the restaurant was practically empty. I was sitting there, confused, trying to download the QueueQueue app. They came over and said, "Two people, you can come in now," and told us to go upstairs where there were other people, about 10 in total. There was no seating arrangement; everyone was just standing around looking confused. Then, a staff member shouted, "Everyone, sit down! So we can say it all at once!" and then shouted the buffet price. It was ridiculous. I just walked out. I didn't even get to eat, so I don't know what the food was like. I definitely won't be returning. I was paying for my meal, not begging for it.
sample_reviews_en.author: NADTIDA NONGKHAI

sample_reviews_en.text:
The price is good, using the story upload promo, all-inclusive for 279 baht.
2-hour buffet, the food selection is quite extensive.
It focuses on meatballs, with every type available, but I felt the fish meatballs were a bit sour. The texture was fresh, but maybe because it's a buffet, the broth was overflowing and didn't look very clean. Overall, it wasn't good, I really didn't like it. Some of the food seemed to have been rotated for a long time and had shrunk. I only ate the tofu skin.

The staff were good, very attentive in refilling the food. They refilled the edible items because there were many people eating.

The crispy pork chashu (4 pieces for 199 baht) was well-made and crispy 👍🏻

**Note: Taste preferences may vary, but I didn't like it. However, if the restaurant improves the quality, it would be better for everyone. I hope the restaurant will consider this.**
sample_reviews_en.author: windy weeya

sample_reviews_en.text: I've been there several times. The first time was good, but the last time the pork was very strange, especially the neck slices which were like compressed scraps of pork. The pork belly was very tough and almost impossible to chew. There were only 2-3 trays of shrimp available, and when they ran out and I asked for more, they said, "We're out of shrimp." The price doesn't include drinks. When I paid, including refillable drinks, VAT, and service charge, it was more expensive than other mala buffet restaurants with better food. In short, I wasn't impressed.
sample_reviews_en.author: Oaoaohh Aphinann

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is a bit small if you go when it's crowded, but luckily I went when there was nobody there, so I had the whole place to myself! 55555
The food choices are average for the price (I chose the cheapest option). The vegetables were good, and the meatballs were delicious, so I gave them 3 stars. But the various meats were terrible. The pork was strange; anyone who goes should try it and let me know if it's strange too. The beef was too tough.
Parking is convenient near Mint Tower, 20 baht per hour.
sample_reviews_en.author: Natchnon Chantachitpreecha

sample_reviews_en.text: The pork was very strange. No matter how much I cooked it, it remained pinkish. It had a weird, chewy, bouncy texture (not the bouncy kind from marinating in flour). The broth was bland and not rich. The sesame dipping sauce was thicker than the peanut butter I have at home. I added 4 spoons of broth, and it was still too thick. The service was excellent. The yuzu juice was delicious; I had 3 glasses. I ate until I was full of napa cabbage and enoki mushrooms (the vegetables were nice and fresh).
sample_reviews_en.author: Phongsathorn Sangsureewatchara

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is beautiful, well-decorated, and has great promotion.

However... the food was not fresh at all. The meat was extremely tough, the pork belly was all fat, and the pork neck didn't seem like lean pork. There was a limited selection of vegetables and noodles, and the dipping sauce was too sour and didn't seem suitable for mala. The only thing that was tasty was the soft drink. I was very disappointed and regret coming here based on the reviews.
sample_reviews_en.author: Phantharee Nidngam (Yo)

sample_reviews_en.text: The soup was delicious, and I loved the dipping sauce the most; it was so tasty I could eat it continuously. The yuzu citrus was also delicious. However, it might be difficult to eat if someone was sitting next to me because it takes up a lot of space. If there were a lot of people, refilling the soup would probably make it more flavorful, as the area isn't that big. Overall, the food was okay, but I only managed to eat two plates of the side dishes.
sample_reviews_en.author: asgsldfhlk ds;a;gl;'

restaurants.name: Shabushi Ichiten at One Bangkok

sample_reviews_en.text:
Shabushi Ichiten is located on the 5th floor, Parade zone, of One Bangkok shopping mall.
- The storefront is eye-catching. The interior is well-organized and inviting, with comfortable seating.
- Food is served via a two-tiered conveyor belt system. The upper tier uses a train to deliver ordered dishes, while the lower tier offers regular dishes.
- There's a section where you can make your own dipping sauces, with recipes provided.
- A kid-friendly area features soft-serve ice cream, where you can dispense your own with various toppings. A wide selection of drinks is also available.
- Overall, the ingredients appear fresh and clean, including the seafood (large squid), meats (beef, pork), vegetables, and mushrooms. The sushi is better than typical sushi restaurants.
- There are two price options:
- PREMIUM BUFFET = 499 THB+/person. Includes Angus ribeye, pork loin, bacon, and Kurobuta pork neck.
- PLATINUM BUFFET = 599 THB+/person. Includes beef and seafood, Wagyu beef, and Katabara beef. Also available: Kataro beef, shoulder blade beef, New Zealand mussels, sea bass, and squid.
**WAGYU (F1) BLACK OPAL (F1 grade Wagyu beef) requires an additional charge of 99 THB+/person.
sample_reviews_en.author: อิ่มเอม TV

sample_reviews_en.text:
I’ve always been curious about Shabushi, but the long queues made me hesitant. Recently, I finally got the chance to try it by arriving early, we were actually the first customers of the day! From the moment we walked in, the experience was great. You can choose between a private table or a rotating counter seat for solo dining. We went with a table and chose the 499+ baht premium buffet (they also offer a 599+ option).

The restaurant was clean, well-organized, and hygienic. Normally, I go for BBQ, but lately I’ve been into hotpot and Shabushi didn’t disappoint. They offer four soup bases: Tom Yum, Shabu, Black Soup, and Miso. We picked Tom Yum and Shabu and loved the flavors.

The variety was impressive. I tried everything I wanted, from sushi and gyoza to prawn tempura — all of it delicious. They also have a sauce station where you can mix your own flavors, plus desserts like ice cream, fruits, and a good selection of drinks, including soft drinks.

The service was friendly and helpful, with clear instructions on how everything works. Overall, I found it to be a fair price for a tasty and satisfying experience. I’m definitely going back again!
sample_reviews_en.author: Naw Hsu Ei Thin Zar (kk)

sample_reviews_en.text:
First off: This place is open, I came here on Dec 7, 2024 and it was open, I have no idea why someone would put it as permanently closed, probably some angry Indian guy.

Second off: This is the best Shabushi in Thailand, though it does cost 100thb more than the other Shabushi’s, the extra cost is worth it though. You order on your phone and a little robot brings you everything you ordered. There’s also a sauce bar, unlike the other Shabushi’s which they give you a small thing of sauce and then have garlic, peppers, and lime juice. The meat is higher quality here, beef seems more tender and the pork is that Kurabata pork. They have soft serve ice creams though the one in Central World has soft serve Hokkaido milk soft serve, this one has a toppings station which no other Shabushi has for soft serve. All in all, I’ve been to almost every Shabushi in Bangkok, Pattaya, and Chiang Mai, and if you can get over how hard it is to get here, it’s the best one in Bangkok and you should go. Though for normal Shabushi’s I still think the Terminal 21’s are the best.
sample_reviews_en.author: Kyle Schlapkohl

sample_reviews_en.text: Please train the new staff. They don't know anything when you ask them or they are new staff, not sure. There were 4 of us. Today when we went, the restaurant was almost empty. There were a lot of empty tables, but no staff to clear the tables. We made us stand in front of the restaurant for almost 15 minutes. The staff just stood there, confused, and didn't inform us of anything. Until the other male manager came out to scold us (in front of the customers). We were confused. When we walked in, the table was still not tidy. Any cleaning equipment was still on the chairs. The staff didn't inform us or apologize. They just looked at us with a sour expression. If it weren't for the fact that my father wanted to eat, bye. Last time.
sample_reviews_en.author: bbest6clt

sample_reviews_en.text:
Only the manager provided excellent service.
The other staff members were confused and didn't seem to understand what I was asking about regarding my food.

I've used their service several times before, but my last visit was extremely disappointing. I ordered food 30 minutes ago and still haven't received anything. A table of three people who arrived after me received their food and finished eating right away, while I still hadn't received mine.

The reason I don't plan to use this branch again is because:
During my 31-minute wait, I asked the staff twice about my order, but it still didn't arrive. And, even worse, the staff served food to the three people who arrived after me!

The kitchen team is terrible.
sample_reviews_en.author: วทัญญู พานทอง

sample_reviews_en.text:
Shabushi at One Bangkok, under the name "Shabushi Ichiten," is a flagship store offering a shabu-shabu and sushi buffet. The place is very clean. There are two price options: 499+ and 599+. The hot pot is a large two-compartment pot. You can scan a QR code for food to be delivered to your table via an overhead conveyor belt, or you can pick up items from the lower conveyor belt. There is a wide variety of dipping sauces to customize, and they also offer ice cream with various toppings. In addition, they have imported beef, premium pork, and special broth recipes.
#Shabushi #OneBangkok #ShavushiIchiten
#100Hroy #MillionHroy #DeliciousRecommendation #DeliciousFood #NotFullNotStopping

sample_reviews_en.text: I ate here today, and the price and service were completely mismatched. We spent 600 baht, but the service was like eating at a street food stall. The staff were rude, bumped into customers without moving aside, and made unpleasant faces. If the owner sees this, please address this issue with your staff. Only the manager (or maybe someone else, wearing a gray uniform) was polite. We can afford to eat elsewhere, but we chose to patronize your brand. You should prioritize customer service, especially since you're located in a more upscale mall like Lotus.

restaurants.address:

Central World, 4, B332/4, B332/4T, 3rd Floor 4/1–4/2, 4 Siam Square Soi 4, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330, Thailand

sample_reviews_en.text:
Udon Tayuto @ Central World is located in the Japan Avenue zone (next to Katsumidori). The restaurant was packed, but there was no need to wait for a table. The service was good; orders were taken quickly and food was served promptly.

The menu features udon as its main dish, supplemented with various types of oden and Japanese-style side dishes. The prices are good considering the portion sizes.

We ordered the creamy mentaiko udon. The udon noodles were thick, not as chewy as expected, and easy to break. The creamy, sweet, and savory sauce with mentaiko was delicious. One large bowl is enough for two people to share. The oden was generally tasty; the broth was clear and easy to drink, and the ingredients were good. The flavor was standard, not particularly outstanding. The Nanban fried chicken was delicious and a generous portion. The hand roll was also average.

The atmosphere inside the restaurant, particularly the back section, felt a little cramped and noisy due to the black walls and ceiling, which were lower than usual. The lighting was warm. The front of the restaurant felt more spacious.
sample_reviews_en.author: Littlepaw

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a menu that combines Japanese and Western flavors. Once mixed well, the creamy and salty sauce melts on the tongue with the noodles. The salty Umami flavor of the Mentaiko (fish roe) enhances the flavor and the fragrance of the Shiso leaves make it even more perfect. It is a dish that can provide a truly premium experience both visually and in taste.

As seen in image.png, the visuals are mouth-watering. Butter cubes, egg yolks, and Parmesan Cheese. All of them are mixed with the creamy sauce below. When you pull the udon noodles apart, the salty flavor of the Mentaiko (fish roe) is really delicious. If you eat it with a small piece of Shiso leaf, it is even more delicious. If you like noodles, this is a must-try!

Creamy & Rich
Umami Flavor
Perfect Balance
sample_reviews_en.author: Thiri San

sample_reviews_en.text: This restaurant specializes in fresh udon noodles, with options like carbonara, beef broth, curry, and tempura. Today, I tried the carbonara and tempura. The cold noodles are a bit firm, which some people might find too chewy, but I personally thought it was just right. The tempura was slightly salty, but the dipping sauce was good. The carbonara was on-the-spot for Thai tastes; the noodles weren't too firm, just chewy and springy, and the flavor was excellent and very creamy. As for the oden, I can say all three varieties were good. The soup had a slightly sweet aftertaste.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pat

sample_reviews_en.text:
Udon Tayuto recently opened in Centralworld. Been a huge fan of udon, I naturally wanted to try this out quickly.

Ordered Kakitama mentaiko udon, tempura cold udon, tamago with dashi, scallop hand roll, spicy salmon roll and some oden.

The texture of the udon was cooked perfectly and I really love it. But the mentaiko is a tad salty and may not to suitable for kakitama udon in my own personal opinion. Handrolls are a delight and really good. What surprises me are the oden. It was soooo good!

Definitely coming back soon for more!
sample_reviews_en.author: Chris Low

sample_reviews_en.text: There's a 10% service charge, but the only good thing was the payment process. When ordering, I sat there for a long time staring at the staff, but no one paid any attention. I tried making eye contact and calling out to them, but no one came. People who came after me ordered first. If they didn't charge a 10% service charge, I wouldn't be reviewing this place because the service wasn't that great. As for the food, the taste was good, not too heavy, and easy to eat. But compared to Tsuru Udon, I prefer this restaurant.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ashi Vlog

sample_reviews_en.text: The service was standard. The appetizer menu was quite good, with many tasty options. However, the udon noodle dish wasn't to my liking; the noodles were quite hard and the soup was very salty. The more I ate, the saltier it became. Overall, it was acceptable, but not something I'd necessarily go back for. It's a good option if you're unsure what to eat.
sample_reviews_en.author: Waranyoo Rungrotenapadon

sample_reviews_en.text: Absolutely amazing! The udon noodles had the perfect chewy texture, and the broth was rich, flavorful, and comforting. You can really tell they pay attention to quality and authenticity. Everything we ordered was delicious, and the service was great too. Definitely one of the best udon spots I’ve tried and I’ll be back for sure!
sample_reviews_en.author: Ern Lim

sample_reviews_en.text:
I ordered the "Cold Chicken Tempura Udon."

The udon noodles were slightly softer than Sanuki udon, but they had a great texture and were really delicious. And above all, the chicken tempura was outstanding! It was incredibly juicy, and the taste was so authentic it felt like I was eating udon in Japan. I was very satisfied!

sample_reviews_en.text: This Thai street food restaurant easily passes the test. Both the Rad Na (noodles in gravy) and Pad See Ew (stir-fried noodles with soy sauce) have a balanced flavor and color, leaving room for adjustments to your liking. This restaurant prioritizes a neutral taste, which is a fundamental principle of cooking. The marinated pork is incredibly tender and melts in your mouth. Many customers order seconds. The order of dishes is well-balanced. They also offer 100% fresh coconut water, squeezed from the fruit and served in sealed cups. It's sweet and fragrant, a perfect contrast to savory dishes. Seeing is believing; you have to try it yourself. You won't be disappointed.
sample_reviews_en.author: Siam Traveler

sample_reviews_en.text: I ordered crispy noodles with gravy from this restaurant to eat at home, and the noodles were still perfectly crispy and delicious, just like when I eat them at the restaurant. The vegetables were tender, so even people who don't like vegetables could eat them. The flavor was so good that it was delicious without needing any extra seasoning.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ja Aey

sample_reviews_en.text:
This is a modern take on the traditional Rad Na (Thai noodle dish).
If you prefer the style of Nai Kiang's, you might not like this.

The crispy noodles are freshly fried every day.

sample_reviews_en.text:
June 13, 2026 - Late Lunch

Arrived around 1:15 PM. No other customers were there when I arrived, and no more came in until I left.

I ordered the most popular small hot pot (150B), white rice, and oliang (30B).

I was asked if I wanted the hot pot plain or mixed, and I chose the mixed.

Once everything was served, I started with the soup. It was a meat broth with a subtle garlic flavor.

The hot pot was for one person, with the stew placed on top of a bed of cabbage and bean sprouts. The vegetables weren't cooked; it seemed they were served raw with the soup poured over them, so they retained their crispness.

The meat included beef, pork, and offal (such as tripe and liver), and everything was tender.

They refilled my soup while I was eating. I was eating the rice by scooping it with a Chinese-style spoon and dipping it in the soup, so I thought they refilled the soup because it was running out quickly.

I paid after the meal, and I handed over 500B and received 309B in change.

Hmm? Was the rice priced at 11B instead of 10B? Or was the extra 1B for the refilled soup?

In the end, the reason for the odd amount remains a mystery.

It was delicious.

Thank you for the meal.
sample_reviews_en.author: TAKEZO

sample_reviews_en.text:
I found this restaurant on YouTube, famous for its beef hot pot and beef noodles. You can also choose pork instead of beef. It's in a location not often frequented by tourists, but according to reviews, quite a few Japanese people visit.

I ordered a small beef hot pot (150 baht), rice (10 baht), and a Pepsi (30 baht).

The hot pot contained tender, slow-cooked beef, bean sprouts, and shredded cabbage. I had imagined the soup would be thick and spicy, but it was surprisingly light and easy to eat. It tasted more like a Japanese bonito broth soup than Thai or Chinese food. The pot was smaller than I expected; I think I should have ordered the large size. The staff were friendly, spoke Chinese characters well, and provided excellent service. I would like to go again.
sample_reviews_en.author: Spanky Kun

sample_reviews_en.text:
I found this restaurant through a social media post introducing Thai local food, and I'm glad I decided to visit.

It's surprisingly difficult to find restaurants in Thailand that specialize in beef dishes, so this place felt quite unique. The beef hot pot was excellent. The meat was cooked to the perfect texture, tender but still with a pleasant bite.

The broth has a noticeable star anise flavor, so I would especially recommend it to people who enjoy Chinese-style herbal spices. If you don't mind star anise, this is definitely a place worth trying.

My personal favorites were the beef hot pot and the beef gapao. Both dishes were delicious and full of flavor.

I would happily come back again on my next trip to Pattaya.
sample_reviews_en.author: Hana Hana

sample_reviews_en.text: Just like the reviews say, the portions are seriously tiny. Even the double portion is smaller than a regular one at other places. The amount is far too small for the high price. There weren't many customers during peak lunch hours, and now I know why... I don't see the Grab delivery drivers that used to be everywhere either... This place is really pathetic these days. I went back after 9 months... lol, it just keeps getting worse. Now, even when customers come in, they don't even bring a menu because they just go about their own business. I endured the wait to eat, but the taste has deteriorated, the portions have shrunk, and the meat is tough... There isn't a single tendon in it. Lol, cutting ties. Complete breakup.
sample_reviews_en.author: 세상속으로 태국놀기-세상속으로가자

sample_reviews_en.text: This is the first time I've given a bad review to a restaurant I've been here for over two years. I've eaten here at least five times. Before, when I brought two kids, the bill came to be around 300-400 yuan, averaging a little over 100 yuan per person, so I didn't think much of it. But today, for the first time, the waiter gave me a receipt. I ordered four dishes, but they charged me for five. When I went to talk to the waiter, they seemed a bit embarrassed. They asked the owner, who said they'd refund me 70 yuan, but I'd have to pay a 40 yuan packaging fee—40 yuan for a plastic food container! I'm starting to suspect I've been overpaying every time I've eaten here before. Let this be a warning to everyone.
sample_reviews_en.author: 025 lu

sample_reviews_en.text:
A local gem I’ve visited twice in a row, despite it being only a 15-minute taxi ride away.

When I go, I always order one bowl of meat noodles and one bowl of rice.

The two prices listed are for small and big sizes, but there doesn't seem to be much difference. Anyway, it's delicious.

The iced coffee tastes like a wowww iced Americano with syrup sprayed on five times. It’s super tasty because it’s hot.

People go on and on about the value for money, but I just want to punch them in the face.

Two of us went and ordered one drink each, and the total came to 410 baht.

Definitely going again!
sample_reviews_en.author: Dominic

sample_reviews_en.text:
Garlic Fried Beef with Rice - The beef is incredibly tender and melts in your mouth. It's perfectly fried/stir-fried, juicy and flavorful with a balanced salty-sweet taste; the garlic isn't overpowering. The rice is beautifully cooked, sticky, soft, and not dry or crumbly.

Beef Curry with Rice - The curry flavor is similar to a curry puff, with a light sweetness. The beef is tender and melts in your mouth, just like the other dish.

The portions are quite generous; one dish is enough to fill you up. Don't order too much!

Parking is available on the street in front of the restaurant.
sample_reviews_en.author: Chiratchaya Harikulrak

sample_reviews_en.text:
The food portions were small for the price, and the taste was mediocre.
Regarding the service, were the staff genuinely willing to help? I ordered a special dish, but they said I hadn't. If they had apologized first, it wouldn't have been a big deal, but instead, they argued with me, saying I ordered the regular size. There were 4-5 of us sitting there, and we could hear that my friend had ordered the special. Instead of apologizing and adding the special, they just went ahead with it. One time was more than enough. If you ask if I would recommend it, maybe not yet.
sample_reviews_en.author: moomin na

This is my third visit. Good service, the restaurant has been renovated and is very pleasant to sit in.

My second visit was just as good as before.... Recommended.

My first visit had a great atmosphere and comfortable seating. The food was average, but the beer was a bit expensive. The staff provided good service. The only downside was that on the day I went, there were some staff members and their supervisors sitting and discussing work near the front of the restaurant, making a lot of noise and being disruptive. We were there to eat, not to listen to their loud work discussion in front of the restaurant. If they wanted to talk, they should have done so behind the restaurant.

Food: 10/10. A must-order is the Tom Yum Pla Kang (spicy fish soup). It's delicious, hot, and really wakes you up! Not fishy at all.

Very impressed!

The atmosphere is nice, the food tastes good, and the service is good.
However… the prices are a bit high. The staff cleared the table too quickly, even though customers were still seated.
The staff encouraged us to buy additional drinks, which we declined. They then quickly checked the bill and cleared away the plates, cutlery, and unfinished food (before we even left the table). It felt very unpleasant.

The prices for food and drinks do not include VAT.

sample_reviews_en.text:
They were having a beer promotion, but there weren't enough servers. The beer promotion ran until 8 PM, but people had been ordering since 7:45 PM.
They waited a long time, didn't get their beer refilled, and didn't receive any beer until after the promotion ended. Then they stopped serving, delaying the service until the promotion ended.

sample_reviews_en.text: Terrible. Almost everything was sold out. The wait was incredibly long. I followed up about ten times. People who came after me got their orders first. They said they were out of gas, or were on their way to buy gas. When I canceled, they said the item was already being made??? So confusing! I waited for hours. Seriously long.

The food and drink menu offers a wide variety of delicious dishes. My favorites are the marinated salmon and the crispy pork neck salad – both are excellent. Everything is fresh and clean. The atmosphere is great, the music is nice, and the service is superb.
sample_reviews_en.author: Rawipan Khattiwong

sample_reviews_en.text: Their food is really delicious. The seafood dipping sauce is the best, and the crispy pork salad is also tasty. The atmosphere is great, with a camping vibe. The staff are friendly, helpful, and have a good sense of humor. The singer is also very nice.
sample_reviews_en.author: Apy ying

sample_reviews_en.text:
The atmosphere is great, with live music. It feels like camping, hanging out with friends, and partying.
The food is good and delicious, not too spicy. They have typical dishes you can order.
The service is good, and the staff are attentive.
sample_reviews_en.author: Chakkapong Ngowcharoenporn

sample_reviews_en.text: I absolutely don't understand the number of positive reviews for this restaurant: sure, it's cheap, but it's also inedible! When we arrived, the waitress was asleep at the table (which we ate at anyway because it was the only one of the four tables in the restaurant with a fan blowing towards it). We were served two different dishes (pork and chicken) that we couldn't finish because the pork was so tough and the chicken so mushy. The sauce was incredibly sickening. In short, we walked for half an hour to get to this restaurant, which had so many positive reviews, and left with empty stomachs! It makes you wonder if these reviews are even real!

sample_reviews_en.text: The salads are delicious, especially the glass noodle salad, which is superb. However, if you don't like a sweet taste, I recommend ordering it less sweet. But the highlight is the fried pork neck; it's absolutely amazing. Every time I buy it, I ask for extra garlic – I wish they sold garlic separately! It's incredibly delicious!

sample_reviews_en.text: This is a pork frying shop that pays great attention to detail, frying everything fresh to order. Their pork belly is a standout; the flavor is perfectly balanced and delicious, making it an excellent snack. The pork neck is also quite good. I'll try some other items on the menu next time.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ophas Kriangsiripong

sample_reviews_en.text: It might be tasty for the locals, but for a European it's too unfamiliar. The seafood is raw, there's a lot of vinegar, and the prices are high. And they'll add sausages and tofu to every dish... We ordered a large crab, but they brought it with sausages 😬 …

sample_reviews_en.text:
Delicious, great taste, and you can choose your desired level of spiciness.
I've been eating here since the restaurant was in its old location, and I followed them to their new spot.

Now, when you dine at the restaurant, you can also win small prizes!
sample_reviews_en.author: Siriphan It

sample_reviews_en.text: The atmosphere is nice, the staff provides good service, and the food is delicious, especially the fried pork neck and fried pork belly, and the mixed salad. I especially liked the white part called coconut shoots; it was very tasty.

sample_reviews_en.text: The salad is incredibly delicious. The price is good. The staff are friendly and welcoming. If you don't believe it, come and try it yourself. The ingredients are carefully selected from heaven. Come and try it first. You can do it.

sample_reviews_en.text: The food was delicious! Every dish was tasty. The service was good and the staff were polite. This was my first time here, and the service was quick and efficient. I wasn't disappointed at all. I highly recommend it!

Neo Suki's promotion is incredibly worthwhile! 🔥

sample_reviews_en.text: This is a sukiyaki restaurant I'd heard of for a long time but never tried until I was walking around the mall and saw that there was a branch at Seacon Bang Khae. So I decided to give it a try. The food is served in sets, not a buffet. It's similar to MK Suki but with a much wider variety of dishes. They have a lot of appetizers and fried items, which I loved. We ordered the crispy chicken with lemon sauce, and it was delicious! There's an incredible selection of dipping sauces, with many different flavors to choose from. The sukiyaki sauce for kids was especially good with the noodles. The highlight you shouldn't miss is the roasted duck; the skin is incredibly crispy, just like Peking duck! Overall, it was great. I recommend bringing the family here. Oh, and you can get a 15% discount if you sign up for membership. On the day I ate, the discount was more than the membership fee, so I took advantage of it! 😁😁😁😁😁
sample_reviews_en.author: kookykiss kook

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is located on the 4th floor near Sizzler at Seacon Bangkae Shopping Mall.

I loved it from my first visit. It felt and had the same atmosphere as when I was a kid, eating with my family. The soup is genuinely MSG-free because it doesn't leave your throat dry. The menu looks delicious and the prices are reasonable. The service is good, it's clean, and there are many dipping sauces to choose from. I personally tried them all – it was so satisfying! The vegetables and ingredients are fresh, and they give you a full pitcher of tea, which I really appreciate.

You can choose two soup bases for the hot pot. Chicken soup is free, and the rest are priced between 49-59 baht.
If you're a frequent visitor, you can pay for a membership card and show it for a discount.

I will definitely recommend it to my friends and visit again.
sample_reviews_en.author: unless14th Poison_React

sample_reviews_en.text:
I visited on Friday, September 6th, 2024. They had a 25th anniversary promotion where you could buy sliced ​​pork for 25 baht.

The soup was okay, and there was a variety of dipping sauces. The meat was of good quality, sliced ​​thickly, and easy to eat in bite-sized pieces.

However, the fillings for dishes with minced pork/bouncy pork, like the dumplings, had a strange taste that I personally didn't find appealing.

And what I found most unacceptable was that a restaurant of this caliber used disposable wooden chopsticks, the same grade as those found at street food stalls. They were not good for gripping the food. Ideally, I would have preferred sturdier chopsticks, especially considering the price is comparable to more well-known restaurants.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pathitta D.

sample_reviews_en.text:
The food was delicious and the restaurant atmosphere was great, but I was rather unimpressed with the service from a staff member named "Pink."

When I called her, she seemed to see me but didn't come over immediately, which is understandable. However, when I inquired about the bill, her tone was unfriendly, which disrupted the overall atmosphere and ended our family meal on a bad note (especially since we only eat together as a family once a week, and we had to deal with a grumpy staff member).

I've already informed the manager and hope for improvements. Overall, the restaurant is excellent, the other staff members are friendly and cheerful, and I would love to return.
sample_reviews_en.author: BWBTTT

sample_reviews_en.text: This was my first time using their service. While waiting for my food, I was served fragrant pandan tea, which was very refreshing. The pork was of high quality, incredibly tender, and melted in my mouth. The seaweed meatballs, garlic fried rice, and roast duck were all delicious. There was a wide variety of dipping sauces to choose from, and they were all tasty, although the tom yum sauce was a bit too salty. The atmosphere and the staff were polite and up to standard. Overall, I was impressed. It's suitable for families and groups of friends. I will definitely come back again because I've already signed up for a membership.
sample_reviews_en.author: Whale888

sample_reviews_en.text: I've seen this place for a long time but only just tried it. I'm so surprised I only just got to eat here! It's delicious and the price is great. They have a variety of soup bases and so many dipping sauces to choose from – I couldn't decide! The roast duck was excellent, the skin was perfectly crispy, and it came with peanuts. I'm confused why I only just tried it. As soon as I sat down, they served a pitcher of pandan leaf drink – so fragrant and refreshing! You guys should come try it!
sample_reviews_en.author: WA AN

sample_reviews_en.text: This is my regular restaurant. I usually eat at their Kanlapaphruek branch, but they opened at Seacon Square, which is convenient as I can easily get there by BTS. I won't go into much of a review; the food is already delicious, and the price reflects the quality. Their garlic rice is the best! The ingredients are fresh, they have a variety of dipping sauces, and the staff provides good service. Highly recommended!
sample_reviews_en.author: Let's Go! Journey

sample_reviews_en.text: I went to the Jas Urban branch. It wasn't crowded, so there was no queue. However, the things that required a wait were the shrimp and the sausages. They hardly ever came out. If you didn't ask the staff, you'd have to wait half an hour for one serving to come out. For example, the sausages only came out once on the side where I was sitting. When I asked the staff, they said I had to wait a little longer because the conveyor belt was short. But other items didn't come out at all; why don't they rotate them? I'm not sure if it's because there's no time limit and they're afraid there won't be enough for other customers. But if they're worried, I suggest putting up a sign indicating how often things will be served. Otherwise, customers will just keep waiting. The selection isn't that huge, considering the price.
sample_reviews_en.author: manow citron

sample_reviews_en.text:
The service was excellent, especially from the male staff member who was always smiling and helpful.
However, it's not recommended for those who get hot easily, as the restaurant doesn't have air conditioning; you'll be sweating while you eat.
The food selection is generally good and worth the price of 269 baht, which is all-inclusive.
For those who can't handle spicy food, ordering it mild is just right. You can smell the mala spice, and it has a slight numbing sensation, but it's quite oily.

For the dipping sauces, I recommend mixing your own. For those who like sesame flavor,
I recommend 3 spoons of sukiyaki sauce, 1 spoon of sesame sauce, 1 spoon of sesame oil, and a sprinkle of white sesame seeds. It's delicious, fragrant, easy to eat, and doesn't overpower the mala flavor.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nungruedee N

sample_reviews_en.text:
I ate at the Srinakarin branch. The selection wasn't as extensive as the reviews claimed. The shrimp took an hour to be served, and it was so salty that it numbed my tongue.
The pork intestines had a strange smell and were bitter.
The liver was green, to the point that no one dared to pick it up.
There was no pork tendon, no squid, no mussels, no duck intestines, no shiitake mushrooms. There was also no water as mentioned in the reviews. Moreover, after the staff changed the paper, they just stuffed it into the holder of the tongs we used to pick up the food, which ruined my appetite. I'd only been eating for an hour because it looked so dirty.
The desserts ran out, and they didn't refill them.
The floor was also dirty.
At 269 baht, it wasn't worth the price.
sample_reviews_en.author: walaipan pangsiri

sample_reviews_en.text:
It's an open-air dining experience, a bit hot and sweaty, but overall okay. I didn't feel bad because the service was excellent ❤️

Some food hadn't thawed properly, like the shrimp and Dolly fish; they were still quite frozen.
The meat was a bit tough, probably sliced ​​too thick. I liked the pork ribs the most; they were the best.

The soup was good.
The dipping sauce isn't tasty if you make your own; it's better to use the pre-made sauces from the staff 😅

P.S. Many customers forgot to use their own chopsticks to pick up food from the conveyor belt.
Seeing that, I stopped eating and felt full immediately 🤣
sample_reviews_en.author: Gawyn L

sample_reviews_en.text:
The price is 269 baht net, with a 50 baht discount every Wednesday (no time limit). It's cheap, but the quality reflects the average meat – thickly sliced ​​– and the meatballs have a lot of flour. The good thing is the unlimited canned soft drinks and bottled water, all included in the buffet price.
(The restaurant is located in Green Vintage Market)
(I was amazed and surprised by how many people were waiting to eat. I reserved a table at 6:22 PM and finally got to eat at 10:30 PM.) I was willing to wait because I wanted to know why it was so crowded. I'll probably only go once. Go try it yourselves!
sample_reviews_en.author: Taweesak Yutthanarangsan

sample_reviews_en.text: I went to the Green Vintage branch last Saturday. I waited in line for 2 hours, only to find the food selection was extremely limited. Other brands offer better value. The beef was so tough you could lose your teeth. The atmosphere was terrible. Shrimp was limited to certain rounds. The long wait for a buffet makes it not worth it. Luckily, the staff were all good. Overall, the restaurant needs a lot of improvement. It's not worth it at all; other brands offer better value. The 2 stars are for the staff, everything else was just awful.
sample_reviews_en.author: smply ke

sample_reviews_en.text:
The food selection isn't very diverse, but the restaurant is always refilling. The dipping sauces are delicious. I chose the pork bone soup, which was decent.
The dipping sauce bowls are large, which I really liked. The buffet includes unlimited canned drinks, which is a great feature, and there's no time limit either. It's fantastic! The restaurant opens at 4 PM, but we arrived at 4:13 PM, so we missed the first round and had to wait for the first group of customers to finish eating. We waited for about an hour and a half.
sample_reviews_en.author: Tae Pakinee

sample_reviews_en.text: I paid full price and was really disappointed that they didn't have any tofu skin. My friend went on a different day and they also didn't have tofu skin or a variety of other items. The pork belly was mostly fat. They should have posted a list of what was sold out that day. The selection wasn't as diverse as I'd seen online. The soup was delicious, but I still feel like I wasted my money; it wasn't worth what I paid.
sample_reviews_en.author: Salapao Sunlight

sample_reviews_en.text: Each branch of Lao Yuan is different because they are different franchises. The Central Pinklao branch is delicious, clean, and has good service. The food arrived well, but it was a little slow because it was a Sunday. The taste of the food was excellent. The papaya salad was spicy, the fried chicken wings were good, the grilled fish with herbs and spices was served in nice pieces, although the pieces were smaller than at other branches. The fried pork sausage at this branch was sliced ​​into larger pieces than at the Central Salaya branch. The Vietnamese steamed rice rolls were soft, delicious, and flavorful. The grilled pork neck salad was very tasty and spicy. Overall, this branch was good. The staff were friendly, but the service was a little slow because it was crowded.
sample_reviews_en.author: tanyalak kritrueangchok

sample_reviews_en.text:
- Grilled Pork with Jaew Sauce 140 THB
The pork was dry and tough. They should marinate it to make it softer. The dipping sauce was just average, nothing special.

- Three-Mushroom Fried Set 115 THB
Average. The coating was quite bland. It would be tastier with more seasoning.

- Vietnamese Steamed Rice Rolls 125 THB
About 4 pieces. Good flavor. Adding some lime juice made it even better.

- Lao-style Papaya Salad (Mae Noi's Recipe) 90 THB
The flavor was okay. Spicy and the fermented fish sauce had a good aroma. Even though I ordered it less spicy, it was still quite spicy. Those who can't handle spicy food might need to specify the amount of chilies.
sample_reviews_en.author: Pat T

sample_reviews_en.text:
This Isaan and Vietnamese food restaurant is on the 5th floor. They have a wide variety of dishes. The food comes out quickly, so there's not much to wait for. We arrived at 12:38 PM (August 31, 2023). There weren't many customers, so it was easy to chat.

The Chiang Hai Fried Pork (140 baht) has pork belly and pork skin, coated in flour and deep-fried. The pork is tender and crispy, and dipped in a Northern-style dipping sauce.

The Grilled Pork with Fragrant Jaew Sauce (140 baht) has a little fat, but it's tender and not tough. It's pan-fried, not grilled, as the name suggests.

Many Vietnamese dishes are delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ponchagarj Ngamukos

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is on the 5th floor.

I ordered Vietnamese noodle soup (Goi Cuon). The picture didn't look anything like the one presented in the menu. The portion was very small, and the broth was bland. It was supposed to be served in a hot pot, but it didn't have a burner. Not worth the price.

- Vietnamese steamed rice rolls (125 baht): The dough was soft.
About 4 pieces. The taste was good. Adding a squeeze of lime made it even better.

- Lao-style papaya salad (90 baht): The taste was okay. Spicy and flavorful with a good fermented fish sauce aroma. I ordered it less spicy, but it was still quite spicy.
sample_reviews_en.author: แม่ ณิชา

sample_reviews_en.text: I've passed by often but just went in. The restaurant has a nice atmosphere. The staff were a bit confused. I tried ordering the Lao papaya salad, medium spicy. I ate it and cried, lol. But it was delicious. I asked the waiter how many chilies he wanted. He said half a ladle. Um, I imagined 4-5. It would be even better if he could tell me the level of spiciness. The papaya salad tasted good, delicious, not sweet, spicy. As for the Nem Nuang, it was okay. It was pretty good. If you don't like sweet food, I think this restaurant is quite good. The price is quite high compared to the quantity.
sample_reviews_en.author: Stellar Thip

sample_reviews_en.text:
The restaurant is located on the 5th floor of Central Pinklao. The atmosphere is nice and spacious.

Service is self-service; you can order food via QR code, but a menu is also available, or you can order through a staff member.

The food took a while to arrive.

The green bean salad tasted good, but was very spicy, even though I ordered it less spicy. The beans were also a bit too finely crushed.
The Vietnamese noodle soup (Goi Cuon) had plenty of ingredients. The pork ribs were very tender and soft, the minced pork was in bite-sized pieces, and the Vietnamese sausage had a mild flavor.
sample_reviews_en.author: Ben Tordamrong

sample_reviews_en.text: The shop is in Central Pinklao. There are a lot of customers and the staff provides good service. Overall, I'm impressed because the shop is clean and the service is good. Many dishes taste delicious and the price is not too expensive. The papaya salad with fermented fish is very delicious. The spicy soup is bland and delicious. I really like the stir-fried rice noodles. It's very delicious. The fried pork sausage is very average. The Vietnamese steamed dumplings are delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: BB KNG

sample_reviews_en.text:
Today, I tried a new restaurant that mixed Vietnamese, Laotian, and Thai cuisine. I'd never eaten there before.
The atmosphere was okay, and the staff were friendly and sociable.
The prices were a bit high, but I felt it was a good idea to bring my mom here for a change of scenery, as some dishes I don't usually try.
The food, like the som tam, came quickly, but the rest took a while because the restaurant was full.
Details are in the photo caption.

• It’s conveniently located along the roadside, not far from Tao Poon MRT station, making it easy to access.

sample_reviews_en.author: Pongpit Pinsai

sample_reviews_en.text:
The shop opens at 10:00 AM and offers a wide variety of dishes.
For beef lovers, this is the place to go.
They have beef noodles, beef sukiyaki, and beef with basil. The beef here is incredibly tender. They also have pork dishes. If you're passing by, stop by and give it a try.
sample_reviews_en.author: Sirikorn “แนน” Toomthong

sample_reviews_en.text: There are many delicious foods. There is fresh fried pork and fresh beef. Each pack is 1 kilogram. It is marinated and soft. It is suitable for grilling when traveling to other provinces or cooking with rice. The pork breast is very delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: Zeed 555

sample_reviews_en.text: Made to order is very expensive. A bowl of seafood noodles with a few pieces of shrimp and squid costs over 100 baht. It's not worth the money spent and it's very slow to make. #Old people make it.
sample_reviews_en.author: สุริยะ เสมาเพชร (เจือ)

sample_reviews_en.text: They give very generous portions! I highly recommend ordering the dishes with crispy pork; they are amazing and so satisfying!
sample_reviews_en.author: Panggg S.

sample_reviews_en.text: I like the stir-fried tofu with mixed ingredients. The three-flavor spicy salad lives up to its name.
sample_reviews_en.author: Mathi J.

sample_reviews_en.text: Excellent crispy fish soup and fried pork slices. Oh, and for a special menu item, Pad Thai!
sample_reviews_en.author: Phavida Vida
