sample_reviews_th.text:
I had the opportunity to visit Khlong Bang Luang Floating Market, and since it was lunchtime, I searched for a restaurant on Google Maps. I found this one with the highest rating of 4.9 and good reviews, so I was confident it would be great.
When I arrived, there were photos of celebrities on display. I initially planned to order just one dish, but since I was already there, I decided to order several. So I ordered three dishes. After tasting them…🥶 (This is my personal opinion):
Tom Yum Seafood 😐 100฿: This Tom Yum wasn't very spicy but it was fragrant. It would probably suit foreigners, as I'm used to spicier food.
Seafood Glass Noodle Salad 🫤 80฿: This was pretty average, leaning towards bland.
Stir-fried Pork with Basil 🙄 80฿: A simple dish, but this was also bland.
✨The chili fish sauce with garlic ✨ was a lifesaver and made it easier to eat! 👍🏻

If you're visiting Khlong Bang Luang Floating Market, you can try this place. You might like the taste!
sample_reviews_th.author: Pood

sample_reviews_en.text:
I checked Google Maps and it said they close at 9 PM. When I arrived at 6:30 PM, the restaurant was closed.

I called ahead during the day to ask for directions. They said to cross the bridge and park at Wat Kuhasawan temple, then walk 200 meters across.

In reality, the alley was a dead end. The bridge wasn't a pedestrian bridge; you had to drive almost 10 kilometers further into a very narrow alley.

Each road was like a slum – extremely narrow and tiring to navigate. Cars could barely pass each other. Even if the food was delicious, I wouldn't go back.

When I called upon arrival, they said they close around 5 PM, not 9 PM as Google Maps indicated.
sample_reviews_en.author: ภณวิสิฏฐ์ นาถรังสรรค์

sample_reviews_en.text:
Delicious food, friendly prices, and the owner takes great care of the customers.
- The stir-fried bell peppers were delicious, and the pork was very tender.
- The clear soup wasn't too spicy, served piping hot, with tender vegetables and pork, and a smooth broth.
- The fried rice had a wonderful wok aroma without being burnt, which was great.
The restaurant has a homie style, with a very relaxing atmosphere.
The sound of water from the koi pond is very soothing.

If you're lucky, you might even meet a handsome Persian-Siamese mixed-breed cat who serves as a welcoming maid! He's so cute and cuddly!
sample_reviews_en.author: Nopnapatsorn A.

sample_reviews_en.text: This is a made-to-order restaurant, mostly frequented by tourists, so it has a very local feel. It might not be as clean as some places, and the menu and seating are quite old. The food tastes okay, and the portions are generous. It might look small in the pictures, but you'll actually be full. However, the staff taking orders sometimes misunderstand or get the order wrong; we ordered shrimp fried rice but got pork fried rice instead. The owner, an elderly gentleman, is very kind and friendly. On days with large tour groups, the wait is extremely long.
sample_reviews_en.author: Washi Kim

sample_reviews_en.text: Today I arrived around 6pm and I ordered some food to take away, everyone was so nice to me. Food was delicious! I loved the fried rice and also the cabbage with pork was delicious!! This family-run restaurant is representative of Thailand: they're kind, smiley, very understanding (I had not enough cash and I had to go to an ATM) and they cook delicious food. Thank you so much!
sample_reviews_en.author: Francesca Bertoncelli

sample_reviews_en.text: I ordered fried rice to take home. When I opened it, it reminded me of the old-fashioned fried rice from back in the day, which was brown and had a fragrant wok aroma. It was great value for money. Even though there are few menu items, talking to the owner, an elderly gentleman, showed his genuine service. The shop felt like home. The shrimp fried rice was delicious.
sample_reviews_en.author: MIRUKU

sample_reviews_en.text:
I stopped by for a meal after visiting Bang Luang Artist House, and I'm so glad I did!

I ate until I was super full and it was delicious!

Seafood fried rice + an extra fried egg + morning glory cost 150 baht all together.

The owner even gave us grapes as a complimentary service~

The atmosphere is excellent, and it is a small restaurant with only two tables.
sample_reviews_en.author: 진미선 (JMS)

sample_reviews_en.text:
Follow everyone else’s directions!

It was delish. For 70 baht ($3.50 aud) I got a Pad See Ew with chicken and a coke. Insanely good value. Insanely delicious!

Honestly, I’ve been in Thailand for 2 weeks and this is the 2nd best Pad See Ew I’ve had (and I’ve had it almost daily)

Came here after visiting the artist house.

Great lil area  :)
sample_reviews_en.author: Madison H

sample_reviews_en.text:
I saw a newly opened restaurant and it looked so delicious, the color of the restaurant is inviting. Honestly, I ate it and it wasn't delicious. The frying was poor. The pork was greasy and the chicken was dry. The garlic topping should be changed. It's not like this anymore. The rice is so expensive. It's not cheap, it's very expensive, but what kind of garlic is it? The soup is... not good. I was shocked to eat just this for almost 200 baht. It was only once.

Correction: The restaurant said they didn't use garlic. Okay, it's just flour residue. But why did they add it? Why didn't they add fried garlic? But the crumbly, hard residue has the same texture as the cheap, ready-made garlic you find at convenience stores. It's not delicious. Why did they add it?
sample_reviews_en.author: Kenneth Moon

sample_reviews_en.text: Ordered food to eat at home. Willing to pay for delivery because the food is not expensive at all. So I want to know if it's worth it. I saw that Chef Toey, a celebrity chef who competed in both MasterChef and Hell's Kitchen season 2, was the one who opened it. After tasting it, the quality of the food was very good. I intend to support the chef who is determined to make food at a price that everyone can afford. Eat until you're full, good quality, and worth it. If you eat at the restaurant, you can get free refills of rice, soup, and vegetables. The chef is very generous to open a restaurant like this. It's really hard to find famous chefs. May your business prosper. May the merit from sharing good food be returned to you as well.
sample_reviews_en.author: Mama’s Jee Jew Juke Jome

sample_reviews_en.text: I saw a video on Instagram about Chef Toey's restaurant, and since it's near my house, I wanted to try it. The fried pork was average; I liked the crispy batter coating. But what I loved most was the variety of dipping sauces, from sweet sauce and chili sauce to shrimp paste chili sauce and Jaew Bong (a type of dipping sauce). I especially loved the Jaew Bong; I kept refilling my glass! It's really delicious. Plus, the vegetables, soup, and dipping sauces are unlimited. I ordered chrysanthemum tea to try; it wasn't too sweet and tasted good. I was also surprised by the wide variety of fish sauces they offered, including truffle-flavored fish sauce – wow! Overall, the food was easy to eat, and the prices were mid-range.
sample_reviews_en.author: PIPIU

sample_reviews_en.text:
So delicious! Worth the wait. 👍🏻

Personally, I loved the fried chicken and the Khao Soi sauce.
It was rich, fragrant, not too greasy, and perfectly balanced!
The crispy batter sprinkled on top of the chicken added a great texture.

What I loved most was the boiled egg. It was perfectly cooked and tasted amazing with the truffle-flavored fish sauce.

Importantly, free refills of rice, vegetables, chili paste, soup, fish sauce, and other sauces – everything was there! Fantastic!

*Actually, the fried pork was also great. Not tough, easy to chew, and enjoyable to eat. But personally, I just preferred the chicken. 55555555555
sample_reviews_en.author: Suchawadee Supapakdee

sample_reviews_en.text:
The wait is too long; the delivery drivers always arrive first. The process is disorganized and unprofessional, even though there are many people and many staff. The person in charge of the queue is even adding extra tasks. They're not dividing the work properly.
(I'm tired of waiting) I've been waiting since 10:13 AM, and it's almost 11 AM now, and I still haven't gotten anything. There aren't even that many people in the store. I've already finished two bottles of water.
I'm so annoyed by the wait. I'm tired of paying and can't even leave the store. It's a huge waste of time.
sample_reviews_en.author: Thanawin P

sample_reviews_en.text: This fried food shop has very good quality, fresh ingredients, and is always fried fresh. Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and clean oil. I recommend the marinated pork and the perfectly sour fried sausage. Crispy and bouncy, not dry or greasy. You can refill your rice and fresh vegetables as much as you want. The soup is well-rounded. There are a variety of dipping sauces to choose from, including jaew, shrimp paste, and fermented fish paste. The taste is delicious and the price is friendly. I recommend it for those who like fried food.
sample_reviews_en.author: Nuttanun Proms

sample_reviews_en.text: The food is delicious, but having to pay for the container for takeout is frustrating. They could charge more and include the container in the price, I wouldn't mind. When I ordered takeout and was about to pay, an employee or the owner (I'm not sure which) said they forgot to charge for the container. I ordered two dishes and had to pay extra for the container. I really didn't like that. They should just increase the price and include the container. The containers weren't anything special, just average.
sample_reviews_en.author: ทศพร บุญฉิม

sample_reviews_en.text:
The fried pork was delicious, tender, juicy, and the crispy batter topping was tasty. The mackerel was quite salty. There were free fresh vegetables, chili paste, and a wide selection of fish sauces. The chili paste was delicious.

I wish they had tablecloths or placemats. When I ordered the regular fried pork, the plate kept spinning because both the table and the plate were so slippery. It was very difficult to eat. I tried putting tissues under the plate, but it didn't help. 😭😭😭
sample_reviews_en.author: P P

sample_reviews_en.text: I was a long time customers over a decade. But this is my first time in 5 years that I was back to this Japanese buffet restaurant. During the past 5 years, I have had many good experiences with other Japanese buffet restaurants and see the great development in this field. However, this restaurant appears to be the same. Food menus were pretty much the same. Food orders disappeared and never came after waiting for 30 minutes. It seemed quality got slightly degraded. Raw fish was just just okay but very tasteless and some tray was already not chilled. Even the quality of shoyu soy sauce was bland.  Coffee was extremely bad to have in an once famous restaurant in Thailand. Service dropped substantially. All in all, there are a number of finer Japanese buffet restaurants nowadays. They seemed to be almost out of the league. Would love to see they improve and get back into the game one day.
sample_reviews_en.author: Chat S

sample_reviews_en.text: the first time i came to eat at this restaurant, although i have been visiting central rama 9 for sometime, in fact many times, just i did not have so much time for buffett, i browsed others' google reviews on this eaterium, seems there should be fresh oysters, and lots of fruits like watermelon and honey melon readily available, but i could not find them and could be i was too polite, eat too slow pace? ! i came at about 6:30pm, stayed until after 8:00pm, but i found many food containers became empty without food or soup refill, eg fish maw soup i like, i.did manage to eat lots of sushi including salmon & others, there were many customers and perhaps that's also major reason that i find some food or fruits i.like no longer available, finally it seems eating here with membership or some kind of  food app enable one to have price discount
sample_reviews_en.author: dr ken chao

sample_reviews_en.text:
It’s Sunday evening, the place is 80% empty, the sushi/sashimi has been sitting outside for what looks like a lifetime, the temaki bus doesn’t have a person working there, the lids of the prepared food is constantly left up, 1 of the soups has been empty this whole time. And there is 1 poor guy cleaning. I don’t think he has any help. And it’s 700+ THB per person. There are buffets like mongkok that is 500-600 and it blows this place out of the water. I appreciate the service people though. But this place is dead.

D
E
A
D

What happened to this place?
sample_reviews_en.author: McLOVIN

sample_reviews_en.text: If you’re looking for a Japanese buffet priced under 900 baht per person, this place really has everything — great flavors, easy access by subway, and attentive service. You’ll find sushi, sashimi, various rolls, grilled fish, pork and beef steaks, hot dishes, tempura, ramen, takoyaki, and you can finish with good-quality fruits like melon and watermelon.
sample_reviews_en.author: Sumol

sample_reviews_en.text:
The service was excellent. They didn't bother customers, didn't even clear plates. If you called loudly, they just walked past. The staff were all out taking photos with the mall's mascot, so there weren't many staff members in the restaurant.
The atmosphere was nice, the restaurant wasn't crowded.
The food was delicious, as usual.
sample_reviews_en.author: suriyanfight

sample_reviews_en.text: My son likes here very much so when he does something good, I bring him here. There are many kinds of sushi, fries, grills...and you can order special menu using your table barcode. Normally we two persons paid 1410 thai baht without discount. I am satisfied with this price. My son eat around 3000 baht value.
sample_reviews_en.author: 아임프롬프롬퐁

sample_reviews_en.text:
The service was terrible. Almost everything was self-service. It was awful. They put out the cutlery, but I couldn't find anything. It was a total disaster.
The service was awful, the worst in the whole wide world.
I went to eat at the buffet and walked around looking for things until I was dizzy.
sample_reviews_en.author: วร ธนส

sample_reviews_en.text: A major Japanese buffet in Bangkok. In the past, it was so popular that you had to queue to get in. Nowadays, there is a lot of competition. The current price in 2024 is a bit over 700 baht per person. The food variety is still up to the …
sample_reviews_en.author: TUUL
